t: Efficient Lossless Compression of Scientific Floating-Point Data on CPUs and GPUs
pb: Scientific datasets are growing faster than storage and interconnect bandwidth, making data compression essential, but existing lossless compressors for floating-point data are either fast or achieve good compression ratios—rarely both simultaneously on both CPUs and GPUs.
me: The paper presents four new lossless compression algorithms specifically designed for single- and double-precision IEEE 754 floating-point data. The algorithms are fully compatible between CPUs and GPUs, enabling the same bitstream to be produced/consumed on either platform. Implementations exploit bit-level patterns in floating-point exponent and mantissa fields to achieve high compression ratios, and are tuned for SIMD/SIMT parallelism to maximize throughput on both CPU vector units and GPU streaming multiprocessors. Evaluated against 18 compressors from the literature on SDRBench scientific datasets.
nv: Four floating-point-specific lossless compression algorithms that are simultaneously CPU/GPU bitstream-compatible and achieve best-in-class throughput (>500 GB/s on RTX 4090) without sacrificing compression ratio.

mx.other: compress+decompress >500 GB/s on RTX 4090; outperforms most of 18 compared compressors in ratio and throughput

th: high-throughput lossless floating-point compression for CPUs and GPUs

t: An Efficient Polynomial Multiplication Derived Implementation of Convolution in Neural Networks
pb: Convolution is the most time-consuming kernel in CNNs and GNNs; existing libraries use either im2col+MM (introducing data redundancy) or FFT (requiring multiple passes), so no single implementation achieves optimal performance across all parameter configurations.
me: Reinterprets neural network convolution as polynomial multiplication by carefully constructing conceptual polynomials that map the convolution problem to computing coefficients in polynomial products. This transformation avoids data redundancy and multiple passes by leveraging fast polynomial multiplication algorithms.
nv: Reformulating convolution as polynomial multiplication to achieve efficiency gains not available through standard im2col or FFT approaches.
th: Polynomial multiplication formulation for efficient convolution

t: Design and Technology Co-optimization Utilizing Flip-FET (FFET) Standard Cells
pb: CFET-based standard cells require excessive tap-cell overhead in FEOL to enable backside interconnect routing, hindering efficient use of BEOL backside wiring in sub-3nm nodes.
me: FFET (Flip-FET) flips the lower FET in CFET to enable direct pin accessibility on both BEOL sides without tap-cells. DTCO uses: (1) synthesizing multiple FFET cells with diverse pin distributions, (2) tap-cell-avoiding placement optimization, (3) frontside/backside wire rebalancing.
nv: Flip-FET architecture eliminates tap-cell overhead by enabling dual-sided pin access directly, allowing full exploitation of backside routing.
th: Flip-FET design and technology co-optimization for sub-3nm backside routing

t: Comparison-Free Bit-Stream Generation for Cost-Efficient Unary Computing
pb: Converting binary radix data to unary representation via comparator-based generators incurs high area and power cost, especially as input count and precision increase.
me: Proposes low-cost comparison-free unary number generation mechanism avoiding comparators entirely. Introduces serial and two parallel (exact and approximate) unary generator designs using alternative conversion logic.
nv: Comparison-free unary number generation eliminating comparator overhead in binary-to-unary conversion.
th: Comparison-free unary number generation for efficient data conversion

t: Dynamic Local Usage: An Accurate Model for Usage of Tile-Internal Wiring in Global Routing
pb: Traditional global routing treats local wiring usage as a pre-estimated constant, ignoring actual wire-shape geometry and packing density, leading to inaccuracies in routing prediction and detailed routing failures.
me: Dynamic Local Usage (DLU) model evaluates wiring usage based on exact wire shapes and specific pin geometries. Introduces tip-to-tip penalty extensions for accurate packing density modeling. New routing algorithms optimize routes according to DLU congestion. Supports incremental changes like pin movements.
nv: Exact-geometry-based dynamic local wiring usage model replacing static pre-estimates in global routing.

mx.other: reduced vias, design-rule violations, and timing degradation

th: Dynamic local wiring model for accurate global routing at advanced nodes

t: Secondary-Power-Cell-Aware Detailed Placement in Multiple Power Domain Designs
pb: Cross-domain cells in multi-power-domain designs require secondary power routing that competes with signal routing; strict IR drop constraints at advanced nodes make placement for efficient secondary PDN difficult.
me: Integer linear programming (ILP) model for detailed placement accounting for secondary power routing; targeted adjustments to cross-domain cell placement; validated against commercial tools.
nv: First detailed placement method explicitly optimizing for secondary power distribution network routing in multi-domain designs.
th: Placement optimization for multi-domain secondary power distribution

t: Clearance-Constrained PCB Global Placement with Heterogeneous Components
pb: PCB placement must handle pad-to-pad clearance constraints and heterogeneous components while minimizing routing congestion and overlap.
me: PCB placement framework with: wire-area model accounting for routing resource needs (power/signal nets); pad-to-pad clearance model; two-sided density model for component and pad overlap; quadratic programming-based legalizer resolving violations.
nv: First PCB placement framework explicitly handling pad-to-pad clearance and heterogeneous component geometry.
th: Constraint-aware PCB placement with heterogeneous components

t: Power-Grid Structure Exploration with Unified Sequence-based Learning Framework
pb: Power-grid (PG) structure design at advanced nodes (3nm, 2nm) is critical for power integrity and performance, but design space exploration is complex; initial PG structures dominate optimization space.
me: Proposes a unified framework combining a novel sequence-based structure generator with a Transformer-based voltage-drop predictor. Learned embeddings from the predictor are used to identify promising PG structure candidates on the Pareto frontier during optimization. The sequence-based generator creates candidate PG topologies, while the Transformer predictor estimates static voltage-drop with high accuracy.
nv: First unified framework combining sequence-based PG structure generation with Transformer-based voltage-drop prediction for industrial power-grid optimization.
th: Sequence-based structure generation with Transformer voltage prediction

t: Late Breaking Results: Utilization of Hybrid Threshold-Voltage Flip-flops for Power Recovery
pb: Leakage power reduction in advanced technology nodes is challenging; multi-VT optimization can reduce leakage in non-critical paths, but critical-path sequential cells resist multi-VT optimization due to timing constraints.
me: Introduces hybrid-VT flip-flop cells where master and slave latches use different threshold voltages, allowing independent control of setup time and clock-to-Q delay. This decoupled control enables multi-VT optimization on critical paths without violating timing constraints. Hybrid-VT flip-flops can be applied to designs already optimized with conventional multi-VT cells.
nv: First hybrid-VT flip-flop design enabling independent setup/clock-to-Q control for multi-VT optimization on timing-critical sequential cells.
th: Hybrid-VT flip-flops for leakage reduction on critical paths

t: An Energy-Efficient Kalman Filter Architecture with Tunable Accuracy for Brain-Computer Interfaces
pb: Kalman Filters are standard for BCIs to predict motion from brain activity, but hardware implementations specialized for embedded BCI constraints (latency-accuracy tuning, energy efficiency) are lacking.
me: A configurable KF hardware architecture with tunable latency and accuracy parameters enables design-space exploration for BCI applications; integrated as accelerators into a heterogeneous SoC, supporting efficient neural data processing with dynamic parameter adjustment.
nv: Configurable Kalman Filter hardware architecture enabling fine-grained latency-accuracy tuning for BCI neural signal processing.
th: Configurable Kalman Filter hardware accelerator for brain-computer interfaces

t: Power-Constrained Printed Neuromorphic Hardware Training
pb: Printed neuromorphic circuits (pNCs) must operate under severe power budgets from printed batteries or energy harvesters while maintaining task accuracy; traditional penalty-based optimization requires hundreds of training runs to explore power-accuracy tradeoffs.
me: Augmented Lagrangian optimization enforces task-specific power constraints directly during training, computing optimal power-accuracy tradeoffs in a single run. Tested across 13 benchmarks with different activation functions (p-tanh, p-Clipped_ReLU).
nv: Augmented Lagrangian training approach that directly enforces power constraints and generates full Pareto front in single training run versus penalty-based methods requiring 150+ runs.

mx.other: 52-59x accuracy-to-power improvement; 81.82% accuracy at high power

th: Augmented Lagrangian training for power-constrained printed neuromorphic circuits

t: A Systematic Approach for Multi-objective Double-side Clock Tree Synthesis
pb: As semiconductor devices scale, utilizing back-side silicon space via double-side clock trees requires systematic design resource allocation and multi-objective optimization, but existing tools only hack single-side approaches.
me: The approach performs hierarchical clock routing with concurrent buffers and nano Through-Silicon-Via (nTSV) insertion, followed by skew refinement on double-side metal layers. It systematically allocates resources across back- and front-side, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and via/buffer count through a unified optimization framework.
nv: First systematic multi-objective approach to double-side clock tree synthesis using nTSVs, jointly optimizing latency, skew, wirelength, and resource utilization rather than adapting single-side heuristics.

mx.other: improved latency, skew, wirelength, reduced buffers and nTSVs vs SOTA

th: double-side clock tree synthesis with nTSVs

t: Late Breaking Results: A Diffusion-Based Framework for Configurable and Realistic Multi-Storage Trace Generation
pb: Existing storage trace generation methods lack the ability to produce realistic, configurable, and diverse multi-device traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies with high fidelity.
me: DiTTO uses diffusion models to synthesize high-fidelity continuous traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies. The framework allows user-defined configurations while maintaining fidelity to real storage patterns, achieving trace generation with only 8% configuration errors.
nv: Application of diffusion-based generative models to multi-storage trace synthesis with configurable parameters and high temporal realism.
th: Diffusion-based generative models for realistic storage workload synthesis

t: STREAM: Spatiotemporal Similarity-based Efficient Approximate Median with Tunable Granularity
pb: Exact median computation is expensive and fails to meet near real-time requirements; existing approximate methods ignore spatiotemporal data characteristics and lack application-specific accuracy-speed trade-offs.
me: STREAM exploits spatiotemporal similarity in data streams to achieve bucket reuse via streaming K-means-like clustering. Introduces tunable-grained bucket mechanism allowing application-specific trade-offs between execution time and accuracy. Uses prior bucket state to accelerate median estimation.
nv: First approximate median algorithm exploiting spatiotemporal data reuse with tunable accuracy-latency knobs.

mx.speedup: 47x vs. DDSketch, 71.2x vs. KLL (10.1x average for both)

th: Spatiotemporal similarity-based approximate median

t: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
pb: GNNs for atomistic materials modeling remain small (millions of parameters) compared to LLMs (billions); lack of scaling guidance limits accuracy and applicability to complex materials discovery tasks.
me: Develops foundational GNN with billions of parameters trained on terabyte-scale datasets; incorporates LLM-inspired training techniques (efficient data/model management) to enable large-scale GNN training and deployment; explores three scaling dimensions: architecture, dataset size, and training method applicability.
nv: First large-scale GNN study (billions of parameters, TB-scale data) for atomistic materials modeling, applying LLM-inspired scaling techniques to GNN architectures.
th: Scaling laws for billion-parameter GNNs in atomistic materials modeling

t: RADiT: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion Transformer Acceleration Leveraging Timestep Similarity
pb: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) require multiple iterative sampling timesteps with redundant computations across consecutive steps, leading to high latency and energy consumption during inference.
me: RADiT identifies data redundancy via blockwise input feature evaluation and skips redundant computations by reusing results from consecutive timesteps. Dynamic Threshold Scaling Module (DTSM) and Compress and Compare Unit (CCU) minimize accuracy degradation while maximizing computational efficiency during redundancy detection.
nv: Timestep-aware redundancy elimination via blockwise feature similarity detection and cross-timestep result reuse with dynamic thresholding.
th: timestep redundancy elimination for diffusion acceleration

t: BS-PDN-Last: Towards Optimal Power Delivery Network Design With Multifunctional Backside Metal Layers
pb: Backside metal layers in advanced chips can serve multiple functions (power delivery, signal routing, thermal); traditional PDN-first design flows reserve these layers for power, leaving suboptimal signal routing and performance trade-offs.
me: BS-PDN-last flow defers power routing to the post-signal routing stage, allowing signal routing to optimize for performance first, then power delivery networks to adapt to remaining backside resources. Uses vector-based IR-drop analysis for accurate power estimation.
nv: Deferring power delivery network design to post-signal routing stage to unlock multifunctional backside utilization and optimize performance-power trade-offs.

mx.other: 90% reduction in Total Negative Slack, 12% performance gain with BS-CDN

th: post-signal-routing power delivery optimization

t: ACRS: Adjacent Computation Resource Sharing among Partitioned GPU Sub-Cores
pb: Modern GPU sub-core partitioning reduces power and area but prevents task distribution across sub-cores; functional units (FUs) frequently stall waiting for results while adjacent sub-cores have unoccupied FUs, wasting compute capacity.
me: ACRS framework enables dynamic sharing of functional units among adjacent sub-cores through two modules: Shared FU Issue (SF_ISSUE) monitors operand collector and FU status, offloading stalled instructions to unoccupied FUs in adjacent sub-cores; Shared FU Write Back (SF_WriteBack) routes results back. Fixed target core assignment minimizes wiring overhead.
nv: First practical adjacent sub-core FU sharing mechanism for partitioned GPUs using dynamic instruction offloading and result routing.
th: Dynamic cross-sub-core functional unit sharing in partitioned GPUs

t: New Time-Domain Preconditioners for HB Jacobian of RF Circuits
pb: Harmonic balance (HB) Jacobian solving in RF circuit simulation requires efficient linear system solvers that balance computational cost with reduction in Newton iterations, especially for strongly nonlinear circuits.
me: Proposes novel time-domain preconditioners for HB Jacobian that address both linear solver efficiency and iteration step reduction. Extends preconditioning to distributed device circuits via a new approach. Introduces matrix norm-based nonlinearity metric for a priori preconditioner selection.
nv: First time-domain preconditioner design that balances linear solver efficiency with iteration reduction for nonlinear RF circuits.
th: Efficient preconditioners for RF circuit Jacobian solving

t: DAWN: Accelerating Point Cloud Object Detection via Object-Aware Partitioning and 3D Similarity-Based Filtering
pb: Point cloud object detection for autonomous driving and robotics faces high computational cost due to complex point processing on large per-frame point sets.
me: DAWN identifies frame-to-frame similarities and filters redundant points through object-aware partitioning based on previous detection results. Axis-sorted point selection refines partitioning for non-uniform point distributions. Efficient 3D similarity algorithm performs point filtering. Flexible latency-accuracy tradeoffs via configurable filtering ratios.
nv: Object-aware partitioning that leverages detection context to enable frame-based similarity filtering and redundancy elimination.
th: Frame-based point filtering for efficient 3D detection

t: Late Breaking Results: Advanced PCB Placement with Irregular Components for Efficient Collision Detection and Routability Optimization
pb: Automated PCB placement must handle heterogeneous components with irregular geometries and complex design rules while ensuring collision-free placement and routability.
me: Three-stage placement framework: (1) global placement with Separating Axis Theorem for collision detection on exact component contours and board shapes, (2) multi-stage force-directed method dynamically adjusting attractive/repulsive forces for clearance and routability, (3) scanline-based legalization resolving overlaps and enforcing spacing constraints. Framework adapts to diverse design limitations.
nv: Separating Axis Theorem-based collision detection for exact irregular component geometries in global PCB placement.
th: Collision-aware placement for irregular PCB components

t: LLMs Meet Post-Silicon Test Engineering: A New Era (Invited)
pb: Post-silicon test engineering requires domain-specific expertise; AI automation of test tasks is limited by lack of domain grounding.
me: Two-stage LLM-based AI agent framework for post-silicon test engineering: (1) reasoning stage interprets user queries using LLM capabilities, (2) grounding stage executes tasks by integrating LLM outputs with existing test infrastructure. Case study: Intelligent Engineering Assistant (IEA) demonstrates autonomous task execution within established test framework.
nv: Domain-grounded LLM agents for post-silicon test automation, combining reasoning and infrastructure integration.
th: LLM-based agents for post-silicon test automation

t: Rank-based Multi-objective Approximate Logic Synthesis via Monte Carlo Tree Search
pb: Approximate logic synthesis focuses on single objectives (delay or area), leading to local optima in multi-objective optimization under error constraints.
me: Framework uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with non-dominated circuit ranking to guide exploration of local approximate changes (LACs). A Rank-Transformer model predicts path-domain ranks, enhancing high-quality LAC application.
nv: Non-dominated circuit ranking with MCTS to systematically explore the multi-objective approximate synthesis space.
th: Multi-objective approximate logic synthesis via Monte Carlo tree search

t: Truly Pre-Routing Timing Prediction via Considering Power Delivery Network
pb: Pre-routing timing prediction in chip design ignores power delivery network (PDN) effects, leading to inaccurate timing predictions. Existing ML-assisted methods fail to capture IR drop and routing congestion impacts on timing.
me: Proposes two specialized encoders—an IR drop-aware encoder and routing congestion-aware encoder—that fuse multimodal data (netlist, layout, PDN) through Pareto optimization to balance utilization across modalities for improved timing prediction accuracy on TSMC 16nm designs.
nv: Pareto optimization-based multimodal fusion that balances IR drop, routing congestion, and netlisting encoders to capture PDN effects in pre-routing timing.

mx.accuracy: improved over SOTA pre-routing timing methods

th: ML-assisted pre-routing timing with power delivery network awareness

t: DCDiff: Enhancing JPEG Compression via Diffusion-based DC Coefficients Estimation
pb: Low-cost cameras cannot support learning-based compressors; one approach drops DC coefficients at camera and reconstructs them later, but statistical reconstruction methods cause deviation-introduced errors that propagate throughout the image.
me: DCDiff uses a generative diffusion model to estimate DC coefficients end-to-end rather than relying on statistical methods. It generates masks to correct image locations violating statistical distributions, suppressing error propagation. The approach maintains full JPEG compatibility with typical low-cost processors.
nv: End-to-end generative diffusion model for DC coefficient reconstruction replaces statistical methods, avoiding error propagation and enabling learned priors for natural images.

mx.other: Outperforms baselines in compression performance; minimal downstream task impact (specific numbers not provided)

th: Diffusion model for JPEG DC coefficient reconstruction

t: 3D-Flow: Flow-based Standard Cell Legalization for 3D ICs
pb: Standard-cell placement legalization in 3D ICs must resolve overflows across multiple dies while minimizing cell displacement; traditional 2D legalizers are inefficient for 3D geometry.
me: Proposes 3D-Flow, a flow-based legalization algorithm that models the 3D space as a grid graph and finds shortest augmenting paths to resolve overflowed bins; uses branch-and-bound for path optimization and cycle-canceling post-optimization to minimize maximum displacement.
nv: Network flow formulation for 3D cell legalization leveraging global multi-die perspective to minimize displacement.

mx.other: 13% reduction in average cell displacement; 43% in maximum displacement

th: Network flow-based legalization for 3D IC placement

t: Late Breaking Results: Customized Diffusion Model Empowered by Heterogeneous Graph Network for Effective Floorplanning
pb: Classical analytical floorplanners are sensitive to initial solution quality; learning-based methods suffer high computational complexity and inefficiency.
me: Proposes a customized diffusion model generating high-quality initial floorplans; integrates heterogeneous graph neural network (HGNN) to capture block-to-block and pin-to-block relationships; introduces guidance sampling function optimizing wirelength and overlap.
nv: Diffusion model with HGNN feature extraction for initial floorplan generation, fed into analytical floorplanner.
th: Diffusion model with HGNN for initial floorplan generation

t: Curvilinear Optical Proximity Correction via Cardinal Spline
pb: Optical proximity correction (OPC) must handle curvilinear mask patterns with complex geometry; traditional OPC approaches struggle with curvature while maintaining mask rule checking compliance.
me: Proposes curvilinear OPC framework using cardinal splines to represent mask patterns through control points; iteratively adjusts control points guided by lithography simulation; develops comprehensive MRC checking methods for width, space, area, and curvature; designs algorithms to fit inverse lithography technique (ILT) results and resolve MRC violations.
nv: Cardinal spline-based curvilinear mask representation for OPC optimization with integrated MRC compliance.

mx.other: MRC compliance; pattern fidelity vs ILT results

th: Cardinal spline-based curvilinear OPC with MRC compliance

t: FactorHD: A Hyperdimensional Computing Model for Multi-Object Multi-Class Representation and Factorization
pb: Existing HDC models struggle to represent and factorize complex multi-object class-subclass relations; they suffer from superposition catastrophe and information loss when handling multiple objects simultaneously.
me: FactorHD encodes each object with a symbolic memorization clause to preserve multi-object information, avoiding superposition catastrophe. Factorization algorithm selectively eliminates redundant classes by identifying the memorization clause of the target class.
nv: Memorization-clause-based encoding enabling lossless factorization of multi-object class-subclass hierarchies in HDC.
th: Factorizable HDC

t: PatternPaint: Practical Layout Pattern Generation Using Diffusion-Based Inpainting
pb: VLSI layout pattern generation requires large, design-rule-compliant training datasets; new technology nodes lack such data, making existing training-based methods impractical.
me: PatternPaint uses diffusion-based inpainting with few-shot fine-tuning on pretrained image models; template-based denoising simplifies generation into inpainting tasks. Fine-tuning requires only 20 design-rule-compliant samples.
nv: Few-shot transfer learning via diffusion inpainting for layout pattern generation, eliminating need for large training corpora.
th: Few-shot layout generation

t: Multi-Partner Project: A Model-Driven Engineering Framework for Federated Digital Twins of Industrial Systems (MATISSE)
pb: Federation of multiple digital twins introduces complex challenges in design, development, analysis, deployment, execution and maintenance including identity management, metadata sharing, cross-DT communication/synchronization, and governance that existing single-DT approaches cannot address.
me: Proposes model-driven engineering framework leveraging traceability as core infrastructural service. Provides conceptual framework for continuous engineering of federated digital twins addressing DT identification, metadata management, cross-DT communication protocols, and federation governance. Demonstrates two concrete industrial scenarios.
nv: Federated digital twin framework with integrated traceability and model-driven continuous engineering for coordination across multiple digital twin systems.
th: model-driven framework for federated digital twins

t: PFASware: Quantifying the Environmental Impact of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Computing Systems
pb: Computing systems manufacturing uses PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl forever chemicals) extensively. Need to quantify environmental impact and identify design optimizations to reduce PFAS use.
me: Quantify PFAS volume in IC designs across process nodes (7nm, 16nm, 28nm) and lithography methods (EUV vs DUV immersion). Compare PFAS footprint across design choices.
nv: Quantifying PFAS environmental footprint in IC design and demonstrating optimization via lithography/node selection.

mx.other: PFAS volume reduction 20% (EUV vs DUV), 15% (16nm vs 28nm)

th: PFAS reduction in computing

t: Enabling a Portable Brain Computer Interface for Rehabilitation of Spinal Cord Injuries
pb: Deploying brain signal decoding algorithm for spinal stimulation to low-power portable battery-operated system. Current implementations too power-hungry for home use.
me: Porting brain signal decoding algorithm from high-power implementation to low-power embedded platform while respecting real-time and accuracy constraints.
nv: Efficient algorithm porting achieving 25x power reduction while maintaining real-time performance and decoding accuracy.
th: power-efficient BCI systems

t: Efficient Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search via Data-Adaptive Parameter Adjustment in Hierarchical Navigable Small Graphs
pb: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graph algorithms use static parameters (connection count M and search depth ef) that do not adapt to variations in data density and dimensionality, causing suboptimal performance across diverse datasets.
me: Proposes Dynamic HNSW with data-adaptive parameter adjustment algorithms; automatically tunes M (connections per node) and ef (search depth) based on local data density and dataset dimensionality to optimize graph construction and search efficiency.
nv: Adaptive parameter tuning algorithm for HNSW based on local data density and global dimensionality.
th: Adaptive HNSW parameter tuning

t: Flexible Thermal Conductance Model (TCM) for Efficient Thermal Simulation of 3-D ICs and Packages
pb: Thermal simulation of 3D ICs and packages is computationally expensive, requiring large solution domains and extensive simulations despite the fact that only specific regions (ROI) contain key thermal design components.
me: The method partitions the structure into Region of Interest (ROI) and Region of Fixity (ROF), constraining the solution domain to the ROI. A flexible thermal conductance model (TCM) with rational expressions represents the thermal impact of ROF as boundary conditions, enabling efficient handling of varying boundary conditions.
nv: Flexible TCM with elegant rational expressions for heat convection coefficients that adapts to varying boundary conditions while constraining computation to ROI.
th: Efficient 3D IC thermal simulation

t: Multi-Partner Project: LoLiPoP-IoT - Design and Simulation of Energy-Efficient Devices for the Internet of Things
pb: IoT devices require extended battery life or energy autonomy; traditional approaches demand frequent battery replacement, creating maintenance burden and electronic waste.
me: Custom IoT localization tag design with integrated modeling of solar cells (from basic models to circuit integration) and electronics power consumption. Analyzes nRF52833 microcontroller and DW3110 ultra-wideband transceiver. Uses publicly available simulation tools. Optimizes power consumption with tradeoffs between photovoltaic panel area, lifespan, and localization latency.
nv: Integrated simulation of solar harvesting and IoT electronics platform, demonstrating framework principles for modeling and optimizing energy-autonomous devices.

mx.other: reduced photovoltaic panel area for autonomous operation

th: energy-efficient IoT via solar harvesting simulation

t: Slipstream: Semantic-Based Training Acceleration for Recommendation Models
pb: Recommendation model training suffers from redundant embedding updates; even after separating popular and non-popular embeddings, certain popular embeddings saturate early and undergo minimal subsequent variation.
me: Slipstream framework identifies stale embeddings (those that have saturated and stopped changing) on-the-fly and skips their gradient updates. Monitors embedding variation during training and detects saturation. Combines with existing popular/non-popular classification for greater savings.
nv: On-the-fly saturation detection for embeddings, skipping updates to non-varying embeddings while maintaining model accuracy.

mx.speedup: 2x vs XDL, 2.4x vs DRLM, 1.2x vs FAE, 1.175x vs Hotline

th: recommendation training via stale embedding skipping

t: Multi-Partner Project: Artificial Intelligence in Manufacturing Leading to Sustainability and the Consideration of Human Aspects (AIMS5.0)
pb: Industry 5.0 requires convergence of sustainability, digital autonomy, and human-centric design; translating these principles into practical hardware and tool implementations is challenging.
me: Comprehensive multi-partner strategy connecting academic AI research with industrial implementation through novel AI-tool chains, hardware advancements, and methodologies that prioritize human aspects in automation.
nv: Holistic framework integrating AI-driven hardware, sustainability, digital autonomy, and human-centric design for Industry 5.0.
th: AI and hardware for sustainable Industry 5.0

t: Linearization of Quadrature Digital Power Amplifiers by Neural Network of ULR_LSTM: Unsupervised Learning Residual LSTM
pb: Digital power amplifiers suffer from nonlinearity requiring complex predistortion. State-of-the-art digital predistortion methods rely on iterative learning control, creating high computational complexity and extensive training overhead.
me: Unsupervised Learning Residual LSTM (ULR_LSTM) performs behavioral modeling of the DPA without iterative learning control; DPD model is obtained via inverse training process. Implemented as a 15-bit transformer-based quadrature DPA chip in 28nm CMOS with Class-G and IQ-cell-sharing techniques.
nv: First unsupervised LSTM-based approach for digital predistortion, eliminating iterative learning control entirely.
th: Neural network-based digital predistortion for RF power amplifiers

t: Time-Domain 3D Electromagnetic Fields Estimation Based on Physics-Informed Deep Learning Framework
pb: Electromagnetic simulation via FDTD is computationally expensive in RF/microwave circuit design. Current physics-informed learning and data-driven approaches have limitations in accuracy or speed.
me: Physics-informed deep learning framework modeling Maxwell's equations through physics-informed loss functions. Introduces self-adaptive scaling factors updating algorithm to optimize physics and data loss simultaneously. Achieves >200x speedup over FDTD.
nv: Self-adaptive loss scaling algorithm for multi-objective optimization of physics-informed neural network training.

mx.other: 14% MSE reduction vs data-driven, 15% vs FNO

th: Physics-informed deep learning for rapid 3D electromagnetic field simulation

t: High Density Si-IPD Technologies as Enabler for High-Performance and Low-Power Consumption Processor Chips
pb: Power delivery networks in high-performance processors require large on-chip capacitance with minimal area footprint; traditional discrete capacitors consume significant board space. Si-IPD (Silicon Integrated Passive Devices) with high-density silicon capacitors integrate voltage regulation directly on-chip.
me: High-density Si-IPD technology integrates silicon capacitors and inductors directly into processor chips using specialized fabrication techniques, achieving higher capacitance density than traditional approaches and reducing parasitic resistance and inductance in the power delivery path.
nv: High-density integrated silicon passive devices enabling efficient on-chip power delivery with minimal area overhead.

mx.area: reduced board space for PDN components

th: Integrated silicon passive devices for power delivery

t: Specialized IC for World-Lock Rendering in Augmented and Mixed Reality Devices
pb: AR/MR requires real-time rendering of virtual objects locked to the physical world, demanding high-frequency pose tracking and low-latency graphics; this cannot be done efficiently on mobile CPUs.
me: The IC combines specialized vision (camera ISP, optical flow) and graphics engines optimized for tracking and rendering. It integrates pose estimation, world reconstruction, and graphics pipeline in silicon.
nv: Specialized IC architecture combining vision and graphics for real-time world-locked AR rendering on mobile form factors.
th: Specialized IC for real-time AR world-lock rendering

t: Hot ChipsKeynote
pb: Keynote presentation; no specific technical problem addressed.
me: Keynote address covering emerging trends and research opportunities.
nv: Vision for future directions in computing systems.
th: keynote address

t: R.I.P. Geomean Speedup Use Equal-Work (Or Equal-Time) Harmonic Mean Speedup Instead
pb: Geometric mean speedup, the dominant metric for summarizing multi-workload performance in computer architecture research, is mathematically ill-defined for speedup ratios and produces incorrect average speedup values that can lead to wrong architectural conclusions.
me: The paper derives the harmonic mean speedup from first principles under two explicit assumptions: equal-work (same total work executed on target and baseline, measuring how much faster the target finishes) and equal-time (same elapsed time, measuring how much more work is done). It demonstrates algebraically that equal-work harmonic mean correctly captures the aggregate speedup for a fixed workload mix, while the geometric mean does not. The paper further shows via concrete examples that geometric mean and harmonic mean can give opposite orderings of competing architectures.
nv: Formally establishing that equal-work harmonic mean speedup is the correct aggregate performance metric for computer architecture evaluation and providing a drop-in replacement methodology with clear semantics.
th: Correct statistical methodology for reporting aggregate speedup in computer architecture

t: CORDOBA: Carbon-Efficient Optimization Framework for Computing Systems
pb: Optimizing the carbon footprint of computing systems across large hardware design spaces is intractable with existing methods because it requires simultaneously trading off operational carbon, embodied carbon, performance, power, and area (PPA) under uncertainty in carbon intensity parameters.
me: CORDOBA introduces the total Carbon Delay Product (tCDP) metric — product of total lifecycle carbon (operational + embodied) and application execution time — as a single scalar objective for carbon-efficient hardware optimization. The framework performs design-space exploration by sweeping hardware configurations (e.g., core count, memory hierarchy, 2D vs. 3D integration via chiplet stacking) and evaluating tCDP under parametric uncertainty in carbon intensity, eliminating up to 98% of the design space as Pareto-dominated. Two case studies apply CORDOBA to real CPU systems: halving cores from 8 to 4 and adopting 3D-stacked logic+memory integration.
nv: The tCDP metric that jointly captures operational carbon, embodied carbon, and performance in one optimization target, enabling principled design-space pruning for carbon-efficient specialized hardware.

mx.other: tCDP improved 1.25x (8→4 cores); tCDP improved 6.9x (3D stacking vs. 2D); 98% design-space elimination

th: Carbon-aware hardware design-space optimization with lifecycle carbon metrics

t: Adaptive Pin Pattern Modification on Standard Cells Towards ECO Routing
pb: Pin inaccessibility on standard cells causes routing failures in deep-submicron physical design, with failures increasing as cell sizes shrink.
me: Adaptive pin-pattern modification (APM) applies three techniques to standard cells: pin-shift-trim (PST), pin-free (PF), and pin-bridge (PB). System selects modifications based on individual cell instance failures and explores routable paths via maze routing.
nv: Adaptive cell-level pin pattern modifications enabling ECO routing with no PPA penalty and 116x speedup over concurrent MCF-based methods.

mx.accuracy: resolves 17.7% of pin inaccessibility cases vs. commercial tool

th: adaptive pin modification for ECO routing

t: Invited Paper: CMOS 2.0 - Redefining the Future of Scaling
pb: Traditional geometric scaling faces fundamental limits; geometric approach of scaling continues to be the only path with new paradigm needed.
me: CMOS 2.0 proposes fine-grain heterogeneous 3D stacking of specialized active device layers enabled by 3D wafer bonding and backside processing. Requires new architectures and EDA infrastructure.
nv: Platform shift from geometric scaling to heterogeneous 3D device-layer stacking as future scaling paradigm.

mx.ppa: expected ultimate PPA gains per future roadmap

th: CMOS 2.0 heterogeneous 3D scaling paradigm

t: Performance-Driven Pre-Assignment Routing for High-Speed Package Designs
pb: High-speed package routing lacks performance-driven optimization that minimizes critical path while preventing wire crossings within single metal layers.
me: Dynamic programming generates high-quality baseline routing solution; search-based method with pruning optimizes net routing order to minimize critical path length while maintaining no wire crossings.
nv: Integration of dynamic programming baseline generation with efficient search-based net ordering for performance-driven package routing.

mx.ppa: 32.9% critical path reduction, 0.6% total path increase

th: EDA for high-speed package routing

t: (Invited Paper) Overview of 2025 CAD Contest at ICCAD
pb: Electronic design automation research requires engagement between academia and industry with real-world problem statements and benchmarks.
me: Multi-month research competition with problem statements from EDA/IC industry; provides industrial benchmarks and solution evaluators.
nv: Contest format providing real-world EDA problems to research community; annual tradition since 2012.

mx.other: 247 teams, hundreds of publications in top conferences/journals annually

th: CAD contest overview and participation

t: Automatic Design for Modular Microfluidic Routing Blocks
pb: Designing microfluidic routing blocks that interconnect pumps, cell cultures, and other modules is a cumbersome, repetitive, manual task, hindering rapid development of organs-on-chip devices.
me: Proposes an automated design and routing method that fully automates interconnection of microfluidic chip components. Provides user-friendly interactive online tool as part of Munich Microfluidic Toolkit (MMFT).
nv: Automated routing method for modular microfluidic systems following ISO standardization.

mx.other: Significant reduction in design effort and time

th: Microfluidic design automation

t: A Parallel Analytical Legalization Algorithm via Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers
pb: Legalization with cell overlap resolution typically relies on suboptimal heuristic cell-by-cell search, while analytical methods suffer from runtime overhead and discrete problem complexity.
me: Parallel analytical legalization using Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) with heterogeneous CPU-GPU parallelism to handle the discrete nature of placement legalization.
nv: Parallel analytical formulation of legalization problem via ADMM with CPU-GPU heterogeneous acceleration.

mx.other: legalization quality: better than existing methods

th: Analytical ADMM-based legalization with GPU parallelism

t: A Unified Design Flow for Homogeneous and Heterogeneous 3D Integration with Fine-Pitch Hybrid Bonding
pb: Existing EDA tools lack native support for multi-tier 3D IC integration with fine-pitch hybrid bonding, leading to 3D via overflow and design rule violations when using pseudo-3D flows based on conventional 2D tools.
me: Unified 3D IC design framework with four key techniques: (1) Generalized footprint contraction for heterogeneous/homogeneous integration; (2) Constraint-driven tier partitioning for pitch-based 3D via budgeting; (3) Timing-aware gain steering performance-critical cells to faster die; (4) Post-route 3D via legalization using reinforcement learning.
nv: First unified 3D IC design framework supporting both homogeneous and heterogeneous 3D integrations with native constraint handling.

mx.ppa: 62% WNS improvement, 74% TNS improvement, 62% via reduction

th: Unified 3D IC design with constraint-driven optimization

t: Half-Height Double-Row CFET Standard Cells for Area Optimized Placement in A7 CMOS Node
pb: Double-Row CFET architecture enables cell track height scaling but introduces limitations on standard cell layout design and block-level area optimization.
me: Half-Height Double-Row (hDR) CFET design style combining: (1) high flexibility on standard cell layout design; (2) cell insertion in backend PnR flow for block-level optimization; (3) feasible MOL process complexity.
nv: First hDR CFET design style enabling both cell-level and block-level area optimization in CFET technology.

mx.area: 50% cell area reduction, 10% block area scaling, 14% projected scaling
mx.other: Track height scaling via shared middle row vias

th: Half-height double-row CFET design for area scaling

t: Efficient Analytical Placement Algorithm with Hybrid Fence Region Constraints Using Non-Newtonian Fluid Model
pb: Analytical placement with multiple fence region types struggles to handle mixed-type constraints where instances from different fence types are allowed in the same region; instances initially displaced by wirelength forces require extra repositioning effort to return to designated regions.
me: Hybrid-Region-Aware Multi-Electrostatic System generates General electrostatic systems eliminating overlaps across isolated systems while minimizing placement disruptions. Resistive force formulation based on non-Newtonian fluid model enhances convergence stability by gently pushing displaced instances back to fence regions.
nv: Non-Newtonian fluid model-based resistive forces for soft fence constraint enforcement with multi-electrostatic system generation.
th: Constrained analytical placement with fluid dynamics

t: Advanced Packaging Warpage Modeling with DeepONet-Based Operator Learning
pb: Warpage caused by manufacturing thermal processes significantly impacts advanced packaging yield; FEM-based numerical simulations are time-consuming due to mesh generation and large matrix-solving requirements.
me: Physics-informed operator learning framework using DeepONets for warpage surrogate model; enables rapid prediction of warpage effects without expensive FEM simulations.
nv: DeepONet-based physics-informed operator learning for automated warpage surrogate model generation.
th: Physics-informed operator learning for warpage

t: Leveraging GPU for Better Detailed Placement Quality
pb: Detailed placement has approached practical limits of CPU-based wirelength optimization; leveraging GPU parallelism to further improve placement quality remains underexplored.
me: GPU-based detailed placement flow featuring Simultaneous Row and Order Assignment (SROA) step that integrates dynamic programming-based row assignment with heuristic-based cell position adjustment; enables efficient exploration of larger solution spaces.
nv: SROA algorithm for integrated row assignment and cell positioning leveraging GPU parallelism.

mx.ppa: 1.35% detailed routing wirelength reduction, 1.03% via count reduction

th: GPU-accelerated detailed placement

t: MF-MOR: Multi-Fidelity Model Order Reduction for Many-Port Linear Systems in Chip Power Modeling
pb: Reducing systems with millions of nodes and tens of thousands of I/O ports is extremely difficult; existing projection-based MOR techniques offer only partial solutions for many-port systems.
me: Multi-fidelity ML strategy combining aggressive port reduction followed by conventional MOR (PRIMA) for low-fidelity ROM, high-fidelity time-domain simulation for limited samples, compensation network trained to bridge gap, tensorized mapping technique capturing port correlations for efficient learning.
nv: Multi-fidelity approach combining reduced-order model with learned compensation network for many-port systems.

mx.other: Scalable and cost-effective, generalizable to different input waveforms

th: Multi-fidelity MOR for chip power

t: ProtoCellLayout: Prototype-Guided Graph Learning for Accurate and Generalizable Standard Cell Layout PPA Estimation
pb: Standard cell layout PPA estimation requires rapid and precise methods; geometry-based approaches lack accuracy, SPICE simulations are slow, and ML methods don't capture layout-dependent effects and require massive training data.
me: Topology-Geometry Graph (TGG) representation integrating circuit topology and geometric features; prototype learning mechanism leveraging CMOS logic structural regularity and routing pattern similarity for generalization across cells with minimal training data.
nv: TGG representation capturing both topology and geometry; prototype learning for cross-cell generalization using structural regularity.

mx.ppa: <3.5% percentage error, >95% accuracy in layout selection

th: Graph learning for cell layout PPA

t: DiSPlace - transistor-level placement with diffusion-sharing optimization
pb: Transistor-level placement directly impacts chip area, power consumption, and timing. Traditional placement algorithms do not optimize for diffusion-sharing opportunities at the transistor level.
me: DiSPlace performs transistor-level placement incorporating diffusion-sharing constraints, using optimization algorithms to identify and merge adjacent diffusion regions while maintaining electrical correctness and timing.
nv: Integration of diffusion-sharing optimization into transistor-level placement, achieving simultaneous area and wirelength improvements.
th: Diffusion-aware transistor placement

t: Orthrus - dual-loop system-technology co-optimization using Bayesian optimization and differential evolution
pb: System-technology co-optimization requires simultaneous optimization of algorithmic parameters, system architecture, and semiconductor technology choices. Exploring this massive multi-dimensional space is computationally expensive.
me: Orthrus uses a dual-loop optimization framework integrating Bayesian optimization for refined parameter search and differential evolution for global exploration, enabling simultaneous tuning of application, architecture, and technology parameters.
nv: Dual-loop system-technology co-optimization combining Bayesian optimization and differential evolution for efficient multi-dimensional parameter space exploration.
th: Multi-level system-technology optimization

t: HyperEF 2.0: Spectral Hypergraph Coarsening via Krylov Subspace Expansion and Resistance-Based Local Clustering
pb: Hypergraph partitioning and coarsening require preserving structural properties while maintaining solution quality. Existing methods struggle to balance coarsening effectiveness with solution quality metrics like conductance.
me: HyperEF 2.0 improves spectral coarsening through: (1) expanded Krylov subspace leveraging clique and star expansions for better effective resistance approximation, (2) resistance-based local clustering for balanced node merging, (3) integration into multilevel hypergraph partitioning with hyperedge weighting and community detection.
nv: Krylov subspace-based spectral coarsening with resistance-based local clustering for improved balance.
th: Efficient spectral hypergraph partitioning for VLSI

t: BAGNet: A Boundary-Aware Graph Neural Network for SRAM Yield Analysis in Post-LayoutSimulation
pb: Post-layout SRAM yield analysis is complicated by inter-column correlations from parasitic parameters that previous pre-layout methods ignore, making yield estimation difficult and time-consuming.
me: BAGNet uses a GNN to learn graph representations of SRAM arrays and generate feature vectors, constructs an MLP-based surrogate model for performance prediction, and introduces nonlinear mapping with adaptive iteration for boundary-aware capability. Uses importance sampling on the surrogate model for efficient yield estimation without circuit simulation.
nv: Boundary-aware GNN-based surrogate model for SRAM yield that captures post-layout parasitic effects.
th: GNN-based surrogate modeling for SRAM yield prediction

t: Uncertainty-Guided Live Measurement Sequencing for Fast SAR ADC Linearity Testing
pb: Testing high-resolution Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADCs requires extensive data collection and post-processing, increasing test time and complexity.
me: Proposes adaptive closed-loop testing using iterative behavioral model refined by Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) in real-time. Dynamically selects measurement points based on model uncertainty to maximize information gain, narrowing sampling intervals as estimation progresses. Directly estimates capacitor mismatch parameters determining INL.
nv: Uncertainty-guided adaptive measurement sequencing for SAR ADC linearity testing.
th: Adaptive uncertainty-guided ADC linearity testing

t: Enhancing Timing Closure via Spatially Embedded Graph Transformer with Low Power/Area Overhead
pb: Achieving timing closure in advanced technologies is challenging because traditional post-placement optimization fails to account for routing variations, leading to persistent timing violations.
me: Proposes Spatially Embedded Graph Transformer (SEGT) for timing prediction at placement stage. Incorporates distance-aware self-attention and positional encoding tailored to circuit geometry. Develops preemptive timing closure framework that identifies post-routing violations and adjusts required arrival time to clear each violation.
nv: Graph Transformer with spatial embeddings for routing-aware timing prediction.
th: Graph Transformer for routing-aware timing prediction

t: Transferable Parasitic Estimation via Graph Contrastive Learning and Label Rebalancing in AMS Circuits
pb: Parasitic element estimation in AMS circuits is critical for accurate simulation but suffers from high variance and circuit-specific variation, limiting generalization across designs.
me: Use graph neural networks (GNN) on AMS circuit netlist representations (AIG/structural graphs) with contrastive learning objective. Apply label rebalancing to handle imbalanced parasitic distributions and improve transfer learning across circuit families.
nv: Graph contrastive learning with label rebalancing for transferable parasitic element estimation across AMS circuit designs.
th: transferable parasitic estimation via graph contrastive learning

t: DeepCell: Self-Supervised Multiview Fusion for Circuit Representation Learning
pb: Circuit design automation lacks effective representation learning from heterogeneous circuit data (AIGs, netlists); learning transferable features is challenging without labeled datasets.
me: Apply self-supervised contrastive learning on dual circuit representations: AND-inverter graphs (AIG) for logic structure and netlist for physical connectivity. Fuse both views via contrastive objective to learn unified circuit embeddings robust to view misalignment.
nv: Self-supervised multiview contrastive learning for circuit representation combining AIG and netlist information.
th: self-supervised multiview circuit representation learning

t: Invited paper - Connecting the D.O.T.S.: Design of fluidic circuit boards for multi-OoC platforms using CAD Tools for Standardization
pb: Connecting multiple Organ-on-Chip (OoC) platforms in a standardized way remains a significant challenge. Current approaches lack unified design standards and connector specifications, limiting the ability to integrate multiple OoC components into complex, integrated systems on a single microfluidic platform.
me: Development of CAD tools and design methodologies for creating standardized microfluidic circuit board connectors and connection architectures. The work leverages design automation to enable consistent specification and fabrication of connectors across different OoC platforms.
nv: First systematic approach to standardized design of microfluidic circuit board connectors for multi-OoC integration using CAD tools. Addresses the lack of standardization in microfluidic chip interconnection, enabling modular composition of OoC components.
th: hardware-design-tools

t: CoP&R: Co-Optimizing Place-and-Route for Standard Cell Layout via MCTS and AllSAT
pb: Standard cell placement and routing are typically solved sequentially; coupled optimization is NP-hard and requires sophisticated algorithms to avoid local optima.
me: Use Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to explore placement configurations while predicting routing feasibility via incremental SAT solvers (AllSAT). Iteratively refine place-route decisions with feedback from routing analysis.
nv: Co-optimization of placement and routing via MCTS-guided search with AllSAT routing feasibility checking.
th: co-optimized placement and routing via MCTS and SAT

t: VeriOpt: PPA-Aware High-Quality Verilog Generation via Multi-Role LLMs
pb: LLM-generated Verilog prioritizes functional correctness while ignoring Power-Performance-Area (PPA) metrics critical for industrial designs.
me: Role-based multi-LLM framework with specialized roles (Planner, Programmer, Reviewer, Evaluator) integrated with PPA-aware prompting and multi-modal feedback from synthesis reports.
nv: First PPA-aware LLM framework using role-based prompting and synthesis feedback for high-quality RTL generation.
th: PPA-optimized LLM-based hardware design generation

t: MuSTNet: SAT-based Exact Multi-Stage Transistor Network Synthesis with Placement Awareness
pb: Complex gate synthesis typically focuses on single-stage networks, neglecting multi-stage opportunities and transistor placement, limiting optimization potential.
me: SAT-based exact synthesis framework with multi-stage hierarchy for deeper optimization and placement-aware transistor network minimization for simultaneous count and area reduction.
nv: First multi-stage SAT-based transistor network synthesis incorporating placement constraints.
th: Multi-stage placement-aware transistor network synthesis

t: GradMap: A Gradient-Descent Approach to Simultaneous Technology Mapping, Buffer Insertion, and Gate Sizing
pb: Technology mapping, buffer insertion, and gate sizing are traditionally sequential or use greedy approaches. This work addresses the need for simultaneous optimization of these interdependent tasks.
me: Uses differentiable Static Timing Analysis (STA) enabling gradient descent optimization. GPU-parallelizable optimization framework allows efficient exploration of the design space. Integrates technology mapping, buffer insertion, and gate sizing in a unified gradient-based framework.
nv: First to apply differentiable STA for simultaneous optimization of technology mapping, buffer insertion, and gate sizing using gradient descent.
th: Simultaneous circuit optimization via differentiable STA

t: ApproxGNN: A Pretrained GNN for Parameter Prediction in Design Space Exploration for Approximate Computing
pb: Design space exploration for approximate accelerators requires expensive evaluation of QoR-cost tradeoffs for many parameter configurations.
me: Graph Neural Network trained to predict quality-of-result and cost metrics. Transfer learning approach with pre-trained model. Generalizes across multiple approximate computing scenarios.
nv: First pre-trained GNN for approximate computing design space exploration with transfer learning capability.
th: GNN-based DSE for approximate accelerators

t: Towards Multi-Objective Routing: A Novel Coreset-based Transfer Learning Framework
pb: Routing optimization with multiple conflicting objectives (timing, power, wirelength) traditionally trades quality for optimization time.
me: Coreset-based transfer learning framework for multi-objective routing. Reduces training data requirements while preserving routing quality. Enables knowledge transfer across routing problems.
nv: First coreset-based transfer learning approach for multi-objective circuit routing.
th: Coreset-based transfer learning for multi-objective routing

t: LMLitho: A Large Vision Model-Driven Lithography Simulation Framework
pb: Lithography simulation is computationally expensive, slowing design validation and optimization for advanced technology nodes.
me: Large vision model trained on 100k lithography patterns for simulation. Vision transformer architecture for pattern-to-output mapping. Generalizes to advanced technology nodes beyond training data.
nv: First large vision model-based approach to lithography simulation achieving 120x speedup over commercial tools.
th: Vision model-based lithography simulation

t: NUA-Timer: Pre-Synthesis Timing Prediction Under Non-Uniform Input Arrival Times
pb: Pre-synthesis timing prediction for hierarchical designs must handle non-uniform input arrival times, a common real-world scenario.
me: Bidirectional propagation neural network for timing analysis. Handles non-uniform input arrival times (NUAT) explicitly. Pre-synthesis analysis on hierarchical design blocks.
nv: First neural network-based timing predictor addressing non-uniform input arrival times at pre-synthesis stage.
th: Neural timing prediction for NUAT scenarios

t: When Semi-Supervised LVM Meets Frequency-Based Critical Layout Pattern Selection
pb: Identifying critical lithography patterns for process optimization requires manual annotation, which is time-consuming and subjective.
me: Semi-supervised learning with Vision Transformers (ViT) for pattern classification. Frequency domain analysis for criticality assessment. Combines image and frequency-based features.
nv: First semi-supervised approach combining ViT and frequency analysis for lithography pattern criticality detection.
th: ML-based lithography pattern criticality detection

t: The Munich Microfluidics Toolkit: Design Automation and Simulation Tools for Microfluidic Devices
pb: Microfluidic device design lacks comprehensive open-source design automation and multi-level simulation tools.
me: Open-source toolkit providing automatic design generation from specifications. Multi-level simulation validation from component to system level. Supports diverse microfluidic design paradigms.
nv: First comprehensive open-source design automation and simulation toolkit specifically for microfluidic devices.
th: Design automation toolkit for microfluidic devices

t: Parallel Non-Integer Multiple-Cell-Height Node Remapping
pb: Timing-aware node remapping for VLSI circuits with non-integer multiple-cell-height (NIMCH) standard cells suffers from computational overhead due to exhaustive enumeration of all node-to-gate mapping combinations, limiting scalability for large designs.
me: Proposes two parallel remapping schemes: (1) parallel longest-path-first scheme that prioritizes timing-critical nodes and enables GPU/multicore execution, and (2) iterative minimum-slack-first scheme that also prioritizes timing-critical paths. Both schemes reduce enumeration space by focusing optimization on critical paths rather than exhaustive search.
nv: First parallel NIMCH node remapping flow achieving 5.58× runtime speedup while preserving placement quality through timing-criticality prioritization.
th: Parallel timing-aware node remapping

t: A Complete Modeling Methodology for Full-chip Parasitic Extraction
pb: As process nodes shrink, on-chip parasitics become increasingly critical, but comprehensive methodology for full-chip parasitic extraction considering shielding effects and process variations is lacking. Existing extractors (OpenRCX, PEX) are incomplete on multiple metrics.
me: Proposes complete full-flow RC extraction methodology with: (1) geometric distribution of ring structures with three pattern types for shielding effects, (2) spatial temporal range (STR) tree for efficient aggressor candidate identification, (3) event-based sweeping lines for true aggressor detection in wire segmentation, and (4) fixed metal density approach to approximate process effects on resistivity and determine resistance per square (RPSQ).
nv: First comprehensive full-chip parasitic extraction methodology accounting for shielding effects, process variations, and true aggressor identification with systematic benchmark framework.
th: Full-chip parasitic extraction methodology

t: G-Contour: GPU Accelerated Contour Tracing For Large-Scale Layouts
pb: Contour tracing for VLSI layout processing and lithography simulation is computationally expensive on CPUs. Large layouts require significant processing time.
me: GPU-accelerated contour tracing algorithm optimized for VLSI layout processing. Massively parallel implementation exploiting GPU throughput. Achieves 90× speedup over CPU implementation.
nv: GPU-accelerated contour tracing with massive parallelism for large-scale VLSI layout processing.
th: GPU-accelerated contour tracing

t: dyGRASS: Dynamic Spectral Graph Sparsification via Localized Random Walks on GPUs
pb: Graph sparsification for both edge insertions and deletions is computationally expensive. Existing algorithms like inGRASS lack efficiency for dynamic graphs.
me: GPU-accelerated dynamic graph sparsification using localized random walks. Handles both edge insertions and deletions efficiently. Achieves 10× speedup over inGRASS algorithm.
nv: GPU-accelerated dynamic graph sparsification with localized random walks supporting both insertions and deletions.
th: GPU dynamic graph sparsification

t: PIGen: Accelerating ReRAM Co-Design via Generative Physics-Informed Modeling
pb: Optimizing ReRAM device parameters across diverse materials and operating conditions is challenging for data-intensive computing applications.
me: PIGen uses a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to model ReRAM switching dynamics with physical constraints, combined with a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) to generate optimized design parameters from performance targets (endurance, latency, energy).
nv: Integrating physics-informed learning with generative design for automated ReRAM parameter optimization across materials.
th: Physics-informed generative modeling for memory device design

t: CorDBA: Corners Decoupled Bayesian Approach for yield optimization
pb: Yield optimization for advanced nodes is challenging due to limited resources and high cost of transistor-level simulation in yield estimation.
me: CorDBA decouples yield optimization from yield estimation using statistical process variation corners and max-minimum optimization on circuit performance quantiles, enabling multi-stage sequential optimization.
nv: Decoupled yield optimization using statistical corners and max-minimum optimization to avoid expensive yield estimation.
th: Efficient yield optimization via decoupled corner-based approach

t: A Geometry-Material Aware Point Cloud Transformer for Large-scale Unstructured Thermal Analysis in 2.5D ICs
pb: Thermal management in large-scale unstructured 2.5D ICs requires modeling complex geometries and heterogeneous materials while maintaining memory efficiency.
me: Therm-PCT uses point-cloud transformer with adaptive multipath-coupled diffusion (AMD) for heat diffusion, wavelet-based fine-grained recovery (WFR) for thermal gradients, and thermal-aware Mixture-of-Material-Experts (TA-MoME) for material-specific routing.
nv: Geometry-material aware point-cloud transformer with wavelet enhancement and expert routing for thermal prediction in complex 2.5D systems.
th: Deep learning thermal prediction for heterogeneous 2.5D ICs

t: Optimal Selection and Placement of Voltage Regulators in 2.5D Heterogeneously Integrated Systems
pb: 2.5D heterogeneously integrated systems require optimal voltage regulator (VR) placement for efficient power delivery with heterogeneous chiplet loads and nonuniform power distributions.
me: Formulates VR selection and placement as 0–1 MILP using macromodeling to manage problem size, optimizing for number, location, and type of switched-capacitor voltage regulators (SCVRs) on active silicon interposer.
nv: Automated MILP-based optimization for heterogeneous VR placement in 2.5D systems using macromodeling for scalability.
th: MILP-based VR optimization for 2.5D heterogeneous systems

t: H3D: Heterogeneous Resources Aware Global Router for Face-to-Face Bonded 3D ICs
pb: 3D IC routing is challenging; existing pseudo-3D approaches separate intra-die and inter-die routing, degrading solution quality by not considering hybrid bonding terminal (HBT) resources jointly.
me: H3D is a native 3D global router constructing heterogeneous routing grids representing routing and HBT resources, using dynamic programming algorithms to optimize HBT number/locations for 3D Steiner trees with reverse DFS and BFS traversals.
nv: First native 3D global router designed for face-to-face bonded 3D ICs with joint optimization of HBT placement.
th: Native 3D global routing for face-to-face bonded ICs

t: MMCircuitEval: A Comprehensive Multimodal Circuit-Focused Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs
pb: Existing LLM evaluation benchmarks lack comprehensive coverage of EDA tasks; multimodal LLMs need assessment across diverse circuit design stages and abilities.
me: MMCircuitEval curates 3614 QA pairs spanning digital/analog circuits across EDA stages (knowledge, specifications, front-end, back-end), derived from textbooks/datasheets/docs with expert review, categorized by design stage, circuit type, abilities, and difficulty.
nv: First comprehensive multimodal benchmark for EDA covering diverse design stages and circuit types.
th: Multimodal benchmark for EDA task evaluation

t: GTA: GPU-Accelerated Track Assignment with Lightweight Lookup Table for Conflict Detection
pb: Track assignment in VLSI routing is computationally intensive and typically CPU-only; existing approaches lack design-rule awareness for accurate congestion analysis.
me: GTA uses GPU acceleration with lightweight lookup tables for conflict detection and holistically addresses design rules to provide accurate congestion analysis and high-quality initial solutions for detailed routing.
nv: First GPU-accelerated track assignment framework with design-rule awareness for improved routing quality.
th: GPU-accelerated design-rule-aware track assignment

t: EI-TR: A Versatile Exponential Integrator Framework for Transient Analysis of Generic Nonlinear Circuits
pb: Application of exponential integrator (EI) methods to generic nonlinear circuits faces numerical instability and difficulty in combining with Newton iterations.
me: Novel nonlinear EI framework with implicit regularization using smart eigenvalue modification to avoid system partition that induces numerical instability; truncated rational (TR) approximation for nonlinear function treatment. Decouples linear and nonlinear system solutions and reduces three-layer nested iteration in EI-NK to single Newton loop similar to conventional BDF.
nv: Implicit regularization scheme with TR approximation enabling stable exponential integration for generic nonlinear circuits.
th: Circuit simulation acceleration

t: SetupKit: Efficient Multi-Corner Setup/Hold Time Characterization Using Bias-Enhanced Interpolation and Active Learning
pb: Accurate setup/hold time characterization relies on potentially millions of SPICE simulations across diverse process-voltage-temperature (PVT) corners, creating a major bottleneck lasting weeks or months. Existing methods suffer from slow search convergence and inefficient exploration in multi-corner settings.
me: SetupKit integrates three key innovations: BEIRA (bias-enhanced interpolation search) from statistical error modeling to accelerate convergence; initial search interval estimation by circuit analysis; active learning strategy using Gaussian Process to learn PVT-timing correlations and guide simulations to informative corners, minimizing redundancy in multi-corner characterization.
nv: Active learning approach using Gaussian Process to intelligently minimize multi-corner characterization by focusing on the most informative PVT corners.
th: Accelerated timing characterization

t: Process Only Where You Look: Hardware and Algorithm Co-optimization for Efficient Gaze-Tracked Foveated Rendering in Virtual Reality
pb: Image rendering in VR head-mounted displays (HMDs) is computationally expensive, particularly for real-time applications where low latency is mandatory. Existing gaze-tracking and foveated rendering approaches impose high algorithmic and hardware costs that compound the overall rendering budget.
me: The paper proposes POLONet, an efficient multitask deep learning framework for real-time eye-movement tracking, co-designed with a dedicated POLO accelerator integrated as a plug-in for VR HMD SoCs. The system exploits the observation that human gaze is concentrated in a small foveal region, so full-resolution rendering is performed only where the eye is looking while peripheral regions are rendered at reduced quality. The hardware-algorithm co-optimization jointly minimizes gaze-tracking latency and rendering compute cost through a tightly coupled accelerator-SoC interface.
nv: A hardware-algorithm co-design that unifies multitask gaze tracking (POLONet) with a dedicated SoC accelerator (POLO) to achieve end-to-end foveated rendering with minimal latency overhead.

mx.speedup: 3.9x reduction in end-to-end latency vs. latest gaze tracking methods

th: gaze-driven foveated rendering accelerator

t: 15.1 A 3.9mW 200words/min Neural Signal Processor in Speech Decoding for Brain-Machine Interface
pb: Speech-based brain-machine interfaces require real-time neural network inference on implanted devices with ultra-low power budgets; existing high-end CPUs consume 65 W and require 5.3 seconds to decode a single word, making implantable BMI impractical.
me: A dedicated neural signal processor that maps the speech-decoding neural network (phone probability inference followed by beam-search word decoding using a language model) onto a specialized hardware pipeline. The design combines efficient NN inference blocks with language-model lookup acceleration to decode at 200 words/min.
nv: First dedicated hardware processor for speech-decoding BMI achieving real-time word-rate performance at implantable power levels (3.9 mW), demonstrating practical neural-network acceleration for biomedical inference.
th: Ultra-low-power speech-decoding neural accelerator for implantable BMI

t: 32.3 An Accurate Secondary-Side Controller with GaN-Based CGS Isolated Driver Achieving Sub-1% Error On-Chip Sensing
pb: LLC resonant converter secondary-side controllers require precise synchronous-rectifier (SR) on/off timing to minimize dead-time losses; conventional GaN SRs lack body diodes and suffer from current-collapse effects, and accurate current sensing at the secondary side is difficult to integrate.
me: A secondary-side controller with GaN-based common-gate-source (CGS) isolated driver enabling accurate on-chip current sensing via a gate-charge (CGS) monitoring technique. The driver provides strong driving capability with zero delay and precise SR timing while maintaining integrated current-sensing accuracy below 1% error.
nv: First demonstration of CGS-based isolated driver for GaN synchronous rectifiers with integrated sub-1% error current sensing, eliminating external sensing components and improving dead-time loss control.
th: Integrated GaN gate driver with sub-1% on-chip current sensing for efficient power conversion

t: 32.6 A Dynamic-RON-Diminished Bidirectional GaN Load Switch with Inrush Current Protection and Spike Attenuation
pb: Bidirectional GaN load switches for 48V EV power systems require both reverse-current blocking and bidirectional current transfer; monolithic bidirectional GaN (Bi-GaN) devices reduce on-resistance vs. discrete back-to-back solutions but suffer from overstress during turn-off when gate-to-source voltage exceeds breakdown limits, requiring complex turn-off selectors.
me: A dynamic-RON-diminished bidirectional GaN load switch using a monolithic bidirectional GaN device with CD (common-drain) topology. The design employs a novel turn-off control strategy that dynamically selects between gate-to-first-terminal or gate-to-second-terminal paths to avoid overstress, combined with inrush-current protection and spike-attenuation circuits.
nv: First monolithic Bi-GaN load switch with dynamic RON minimization and integrated overstress protection, achieving both efficient bidirectional switching and reliable gate-drive without complex external selectors.
th: Bidirectional GaN load switch with dynamic RON control for 48V EV power systems

t: 3.1 A 121.3dB-DR, 115dB-PSNR, Digital-Input Capacitive-Feedback Class-D Audio Amplifier with Double-Sided Voltage-Boosting (DSVB) Modulation
pb: Class-D audio amplifiers are limited in output power by battery voltage; prior approaches achieve boost via 2-stage DC-DC conversion (inefficient, ~80%) or single-stage buck-boost (limited dynamic range), struggling to combine high dynamic range (>120dB) with high efficiency and small form-factor.
me: Double-sided voltage-boosting (DSVB) modulation integrating capacitive-feedback chopper-amplifier with single-inductor buck-boost power stage, achieving high dynamic range (121.3dB DR) with 87% efficiency and only one off-chip inductor via single-stage power delivery.
nv: Single-inductor DSVB scheme combining capacitive-feedback noise elimination with buck-boost voltage boosting for simultaneous high DR and high efficiency.
th: Ultra-high-DR Class-D audio amplifier with single-inductor boost.

t: 34.2 A 380μW and -242.8dB FoM Digital-PLL-Based GFSK Modulator with Sub-20μs Settling Frequency Hopping for Bluetooth Low-Energy in 22nm CMOS
pb: Ultra-low-power Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) transceivers must support GFSK modulation and adaptive frequency hopping (2.402-2.480GHz) with sub-20μs settling time while minimizing power dissipation, but existing DPLL-based approaches struggle with the power/noise/hopping-speed trade-off.
me: Digital-PLL-based GFSK modulator using dynamic-tuning-curve tracking and optimized DCO design to manage frequency modulation, hopping, and PVT variations with reduced switched-capacitor banks, achieving 380μW power at -242.8dB FoM with sub-20μs frequency hopping.
nv: Adaptive DCO switched-capacitor bank optimization reducing capacitive load while supporting fast frequency hopping via practical tuning-curve convergence.
th: Ultra-low-power DPLL-based BLE transceiver.

t: 20.11 A Crystal-Less BodyID with an Asynchronous Clockless Leakage-Powered Wake-Up Receiver and Over-the-Channel Clock Recovery
pb: Wake-up receivers for ultra-low-power wearables traditionally require always-running clocks and external crystal oscillators for sampling and correlation, consuming unnecessary idle power, adding size/cost, and requiring ULP oscillator with external calibration reference.
me: Asynchronous clockless wake-up receiver design leveraging over-the-channel clock recovery from incoming RF signal to enable direct digital correlation without always-running oscillator, powered by device leakage during idle state, eliminating need for external crystal reference.
nv: Clockless asynchronous design using in-band clock recovery to eliminate crystal oscillator and always-running clock, enabling full battery-less operation at leakage power levels.
th: Crystal-less asynchronous wake-up receiver.

t: A PVT-Robust 5.5GHz Fractional-N Cascaded RO-Based Digital PLL with Voltage-Domain Feedforward Noise Cancellation
pb: Ring-oscillator (RO)-based digital PLLs (DPLLs) offer compactness and immunity to magnetic coupling but suffer from high phase noise limited by quantization noise (Q-noise) and RO phase-noise (PN_RO). Prior PN-suppression techniques are prone to PVT variations, energy inefficient, or require complex correlation-based calibration of gain and threshold delays.
me: Fractional-N cascaded RO-DPLL using time-to-voltage converter (TVC) and ADC for PVT-robust Q-noise quantization, combined with voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation (V-FFNC) eliminating gain-calibration need, achieving 290.8fs rms jitter at 5.5GHz with <7.5% jitter deviation across PVT.
nv: Voltage-domain feedforward noise cancellation enabling PVT-robust PN suppression without correlation-based gain calibration, reducing power and complexity.
th: PVT-robust RO-based fractional-N DPLL.

t: 5.5 An Ultra-Compact Wideband Load-Insensitive Complex-Cascode LC-Neutralized Power Amplifier for 4:1-VSWR-Resilient Operations in Large-Scale Phased Arrays
pb: Large-scale mm-wave phased arrays suffer from mutual antenna coupling causing antenna impedance variations across frequency, scanning angle (>60°), and array location, resulting in 4:1 voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR) that degrades power amplifier (PA) output power, gain flatness, efficiency, and complicates array calibration.
me: Ultra-compact wideband PA using complex-cascode LC-neutralization topology achieving load-insensitive operation across 4:1 VSWR range, maintaining flat gain, OP1dB, and efficiency across frequency and scanning angle variations.
