t: Generative Latent Diffusion for Efficient Spatiotemporal Data Reduction
pb: Generative models offer compression but lack controllability and reconstruction accuracy for practical data compression; existing compressors (SZ3) have limited compression ratios
me: Latent diffusion combining VAE with conditional diffusion model; compresses keyframes into latent space for interpolation of remaining frames; eliminates per-frame latent storage
nv: First to combine VAE+diffusion for spatiotemporal compression; keyframe-only latent storage achieves higher compression ratios than prior generative methods
th: Data Compression with Generative Models

t: Beyond End-to-End: Understanding the Limits of LLMs in Scientific Problem Solving
pb: Existing multimodal LLM (MLLM) benchmarks for scientific question answering are end-to-end only, making it difficult to identify where and why models fail. Models fail on high-resolution visual data without scripting or tool use.
me: Design evaluation framework decomposing scientific question answering into subtasks (e.g., mapping coordinates, computing pixel positions). Evaluate Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct on high-resolution visual data.
nv: Decomposition of end-to-end scientific QA into fine-grained subtasks to expose reasoning bottlenecks and integration failures in MLLMs.

mx.primary: End-to-end reasoning accuracy and integration failures
mx.secondary: Per-subtask accuracy on coordinate mapping and pixel computation

th: MLLM Reasoning Bottlenecks in Scientific Tasks

t: Assessing Page Reclamation Mechanisms for Linux
pb: Understanding and quantifying the performance characteristics of Linux page reclamation policies remains challenging. Need for comprehensive analysis of decision-making overhead and reclamation effectiveness.
me: Lightweight profiler to measure decision overhead and reclamation effectiveness of Linux's Two-Queue LRU (2QLRU) and Multi-Generational LRU (MGLRU) policies. Evaluation across seven diverse applications under various memory constraints.
nv: Comprehensive analysis of MGLRU versus 2QLRU with lightweight profiling of both decision overhead and reclamation effectiveness.
wl: Seven diverse applications under memory constraints
th: Linux Page Reclamation Policy Analysis

t: DHAP: Towards Efficient OLAP in a Disaggregated and Heterogeneous Environment
pb: Data systems lack adequate support for combining two key datacenter trends: hardware disaggregation and heterogeneous accelerators. Existing systems handle only homogeneous disaggregated CPUs or heterogeneous accelerators within monolithic servers.
me: End-to-end framework with query compiler and specialized runtime. Compiler's planning module identifies efficient execution plans; lower levels generate code for heterogeneous backends. Runtime handles inter-stage pipelined execution, minimizes communication costs, and respects local memory constraints.
nv: First framework addressing both disaggregation and heterogeneous accelerators simultaneously for OLAP workloads through co-designed compiler and runtime.
th: Query Processing in Disaggregated Heterogeneous Datacenters

t: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper C.A.T.S.: Memory and Control Flow Tracing for Whole-Program Performance Analysis
pb: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility assessment for performance analysis tracing tool.
me: Artifact evaluation as part of SC25 Reproducibility Initiative. Reviewer conducted evaluation of artifact description and evaluation appendix.
nv: Reproducibility report for performance tracing tool C.A.T.S.
th: Performance Analysis Tool Artifact Evaluation

t: Porting a Fortran plasma simulation to Exascale on AMD GPUs using both OpenMP and Kokkos
pb: Porting legacy Fortran HPC codes to GPU requires significant effort. OpenMP offloading provides good speedups for most code but becomes bottleneck on performance-critical components.
me: Two-phase porting of Gysela turbulence simulation: (1) OpenMP offloading for broad code coverage, (2) Kokkos C++ rewrite for performance-critical collision operator. Benchmarked on AMD Genoa CPU, MI250X GPU, and MI300A APU on Adastra machine.
nv: Practical hybrid porting strategy combining OpenMP and Kokkos for exascale GPU migration, with detailed performance analysis.
th: Hybrid GPU Porting Strategy for Plasma Simulation

t: eCounter: Inline Per-IP Network Monitoring at Millisecond Resolution via eBPF
pb: Scientific data acquisition needs sub-millisecond network telemetry; existing tools lack fine-grained observability
me: eBPF-based inline telemetry agent; per-IP per-protocol categorization; millisecond-resolution exports
nv: Sub-millisecond telemetry via eBPF; hardware-agnostic per-IP monitoring; low CPU overhead (4%)
th: Network & Systems Monitoring

t: CAMEO: A Co-design Architecture for Multi-objective Energy System Optimization
pb: Energy system co-design requires orchestrating heterogeneous components; monolithic solvers lack modularity
me: CAMEO: DAG-based modular workflow framework; JSON specs; containerized components; Nextflow orchestration
nv: Plugin-and-play modular co-design framework; standardized component interfaces; diverse use cases
th: Workflow Management & Software Infrastructure

t: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper SIGMo: High-Throughput Batched Subgraph Isomorphism on GPUs for Molecular Matching
pb: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility verification of GPU-accelerated subgraph isomorphism for molecular matching
me: Artifact evaluation and testing following SC25 Reproducibility Initiative standards
nv: Batched subgraph isomorphism implementation optimized for GPU execution
th: Reproducibility and Artifact Evaluation

t: Exploring Distributed Vector Databases Performance on HPC Platforms: A Study with Qdrant
pb: Vector databases enable similarity search critical for RAG-augmented LLMs, but their performance characteristics on HPC systems are unknown; little data on how they scale across multiple nodes
me: Empirical study of Qdrant distributed vector database on Polaris supercomputer (Argonne ALCF); biological text workload from BV-BRC; embeddings from peS2o corpus using Qwen3-Embedding-4B; evaluation of insertion, index construction, and query latency with up to 32 workers
nv: First characterization of vector database performance on HPC platforms with realistic biotext workload and practical lessons from deployment experience

mx.primary: Query latency, insertion throughput, index construction time
mx.workload_size: peS2o corpus embeddings (size not specified in abstract)

th: Vector Database Performance on HPC Systems

t: Hybrid GPU Programming Education with Python and C++: Preferences, Performance and Common Python Pitfalls
pb: GPU programming education faces language choice trade-offs; students prefer familiar languages but may face performance barriers; Python-specific pitfalls in GPU contexts are not well documented
me: Course evaluation with 19 CS students (Bachelor's and Master's levels); dual-language design (Python/Numba vs C++/CUDA); pre-course knowledge assessment; performance measurement; analysis of Python-specific errors and pitfalls
nv: First comprehensive study of dual-language GPU programming education, including quantification of Python-specific pitfalls and their impact on student outcomes

mx.secondary: Performance differences between Python and C++

th: GPU Programming Education and Language Accessibility

t: Towards Efficient Load Balancing BFS on GPUs: One Code for AMD, Intel & Nvidia
pb: Breadth-first search (BFS) on GPUs suffers from poor load balancing and memory access patterns; writing efficient BFS for heterogeneous GPUs (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel) requires multiple codebases
me: Three GPU-based load-balancing methods using Intel oneAPI/SYCL: (1) work-group localisation for efficient data access, (2) even workload distribution for higher GPU occupancy, (3) hybrid strided-access for heuristic balancing; unified codebase for AMD MI300X, Intel Max 1550, NVIDIA A100
nv: First unified BFS implementation achieving high performance and portability across AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA GPUs using SYCL; novel load-balancing strategies enabling competitive performance

mx.scalability: Handles RMAT graphs up to scale 29

th: Portable GPU Programming for Graph Algorithms

t: TENSORMD: Accelerating Molecular Dynamics with a High-Performance Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
pb: Molecular dynamics simulations using machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) suffer from suboptimal performance when using general-purpose ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) because these frameworks are not optimized for the computational patterns and diversity of HPC+AI workloads.
me: TensorMD is a custom MLIP implementation decoupled from existing ML tools, enabling domain-specific optimizations tailored to the computational patterns of molecular dynamics. The approach identifies optimization opportunities unique to HPC+AI that general frameworks cannot exploit.
nv: MLIP implementation independent of general-purpose ML frameworks, enabling hardware-aware optimizations specific to HPC molecular dynamics workloads.
th: Domain-specific acceleration for scientific computing

t: ASCRIBE-XR: Extended Reality for Visualization of Scientific Images
pb: Scientific data visualization from experiments, particularly 3D dense arrays and mesh files, is challenging at scale. Traditional tools lack immersive exploration, multi-user collaboration, and integration with remote HPC resources.
me: ASCRIBE-XR is a VR application built on Godot engine integrating: (1) local VR rendering for immersive exploration, (2) HPC integration for remote large-scale data processing with streaming results, (3) WebRTC+MQTT multi-user capabilities for real-time collaborative visualization.
nv: System-level integration of VR, HPC, and AI-driven object modeling for scientific visualization with multi-user collaboration support.
th: Immersive scientific visualization and HPC integration

t: An Interactive Agentic HPC Tutor for Lesson Planning, Teaching, and Assessment
pb: HPC education requires expertise in parallel programming, but teaching resources are limited and personalized instruction at scale is challenging. Traditional approaches require manual code development and external APIs.
me: Multi-agent tutoring system with locally hosted LLM models running on leadership-class supercomputers. Each agent has a narrow role: lesson planning, concept explanation, code scaffolding, and execution. Structured prompts compose complex workflows. Per-agent history summarization prevents context overflow.
nv: First prompt-driven multi-agent HPC tutor deployed on HPC systems themselves, enabling dynamic, personalized learning without external APIs or proprietary services.
th: AI-driven HPC education and skill development

t: Efficient Embedding Initialization via Dominant Eigenvector Projections
pb: Embedding layers in deep learning require training to transform high-dimensional sparse data into compact representations. Growing datasets and model sizes make this computationally expensive in both training time and memory.
me: Scalable embedding initialization using spectral dimensionality reduction via dominant eigenvector projections. Applies MIRAMns (Multiple Implicitly Restarted Arnoldi Method with Nested Subspaces) to extract principal directions from covariance and co-occurrence matrices. Inherently parallel and requires few tunable parameters.
nv: Spectral initialization for embeddings via MIRA methods, enabling efficient parallel extraction of informative directions from large sparse data.

mx.accuracy: comparable or better to standard embeddings

th: Efficient deep learning training via spectral initialization

t: Parallel Rank-Adaptive Higher Order Orthogonal Iteration
pb: Tucker decomposition is useful for compressing large tensors, but existing algorithms have fixed rank requirements that may not match actual data compressibility. Rank selection and tensor decomposition at scale are computationally expensive.
me: Rank-adaptive modification to HOOI (Higher Order Orthogonal Iteration) that determines Tucker ranks adaptively subject to fixed approximation error targets. Optimizations reduce per-iteration cost. Parallel implementation using thousands of cores for large dense datasets.
nv: Parallel rank-adaptive HOOI enabling automatic rank determination with competitive or superior compression ratios compared to fixed-rank methods like STHOSVD.
th: Efficient tensor compression for scientific data

t: From Path-Aware to Application-Aware Source Routing using Traffic Classes
pb: Traffic engineering (TE) must make difficult decisions about capacity planning, flow allocation, and traffic splitting among paths to minimize congestion. Source routing enables fine-grained control but traditional approaches lack application-aware decision making.
me: Extends source routing (PolKA) with traffic classification at the network edge. Develops traffic class patterns and queuing methods for fair allocation across classes. Leverages in-band network telemetry (INT) and P4 programmability for classification and routing decisions.
nv: Integration of edge traffic classification with source routing for application-aware flow allocation and improved network utilization.
th: Application-aware software-defined networking

nv: Reproducibility report documenting artifact evaluation methodology and findings.
th: Research Reproducibility & Artifact Evaluation

t: Modeling the Carbon Footprint of HPC: The Top 500 and EasyC
pb: HPC carbon emissions are significant for climate change, but accurate carbon accounting for HPC systems is missing. GHG protocol methodologies are difficult to apply to individual systems and infeasible for system collections. No HPC-wide carbon reporting exists.
me: Develops EasyC tool for carbon footprint modeling with limited data availability. Uses publicly available Top500.org data to model operational and embodied carbon for HPC systems. Provides coverage of 391 systems (operational carbon) and 283 systems (embodied carbon). Uses interpolation to estimate carbon footprint for entire Top 500 list. Projects carbon trajectory through 2030.
nv: First comprehensive carbon footprint assessment of Top 500 HPC systems; EasyC tool enabling carbon modeling with minimal data requirements; projection methodology for future carbon impact.
th: HPC Sustainability & Carbon Footprint Assessment

t: On the Performance and Scalability of Cloud Supercomputers: Insights from Eagle and Reindeer
pb: Cloud-based supercomputers (Azure Eagle, Reindeer) represent new HPC models, but their performance and scalability characteristics remain poorly understood. Misconceptions exist about virtualization overhead and cloud performance vs. bare-metal systems.
me: Comparative analysis of two Azure cloud supercomputers: Eagle (ranked 3 on Top500, 14,400 H100 GPUs) and Reindeer (ranked 32 on Top500, 960 H200 GPUs). Uses microbenchmarks, synthetic workloads, and scientific workflows including HPL. Evaluates computational efficiency, scaling, communication bandwidth, network latency, and virtualization overhead. Compares against bare-metal on-premises systems.
nv: First systematic performance comparison of cloud-based supercomputers against bare-metal systems; quantifies virtualization overhead impact; demonstrates competitive cloud HPC performance.

mx.communication: Comparable to bare-metal latencies, better throughput

th: Cloud-Based Supercomputing Performance Analysis

t: On the Compressibility of Floating-Point Data in Posit and IEEE-754 Representation
pb: The compressibility of posit floating-point format versus IEEE 754 is unknown, limiting understanding of posit's practical benefits for storage-intensive HPC applications.
me: Comparative evaluation of 5 general-purpose lossless compressors (bzip2, XZ, etc.) and new algorithms synthesized via LC framework. 14 single-precision datasets from SDR-Bench suite encoded in both float and posit format. Analysis of compression ratios and compressor performance.
nv: First empirical study comparing compression ratios of posit vs. IEEE 754 encoding across multiple general-purpose and specialized compression algorithms.
th: Floating-point format comparison for data compression

t: AI Agents for Enabling Autonomous Experiments at ORNL's HPC and Manufacturing User Facilities
pb: Scientific experimentation across heterogeneous HPC and manufacturing facilities requires manual coordination, limiting throughput and hindering rapid iteration. Lack of automation prevents tight coupling between experimental and computational workflows.
me: Modular AI-agent architecture integrating: (1) natural language interface via LLM, (2) multi-agent framework for decision-making, (3) programmable facility APIs, (4) provenance-aware workflow infrastructure. Demonstrated on additive manufacturing experiments with real-time HPC coordination.
nv: End-to-end autonomous experimentation system orchestrating HPC and manufacturing facilities via AI agents with near real-time feedback and adaptive workflows.
wl: Additive manufacturing experiments with HPC simulation
th: AI-driven autonomous scientific experimentation

t: A Data-Size Adaptive Approach to I/O of Poorly Load Balanced In Situ Data Extracts
pb: Parallel I/O performance degrades under load imbalance when output sizes and data distribution vary significantly over time, limiting throughput in in situ visualization pipelines.
me: Data-size based aggregation strategy for ADIOS2 BP5 engine. Instead of grouping writers by compute node assignment, dynamically balances subfile sizes according to per-process data volume. Evaluated on synthetic workloads with low and severe load imbalance.
nv: First data-size aware aggregation strategy for parallel I/O in ADIOS2, addressing load imbalance in in situ data extraction.
th: Adaptive parallel I/O for unbalanced workloads

t: FZModules: A Heterogeneous Computing Framework for Customizable Scientific Data Compression Pipelines
pb: Scientific data volumes overwhelm storage and bandwidth, requiring lossy compression. Existing GPU compressors hard-code fused kernels, hindering rapid optimization and domain-tailored pipeline design. No systematic framework for custom pipeline assembly.
me: FZModules framework provides high-performance heterogeneous modules (CPU, GPU) with clean interfaces for compression pipeline assembly. Asynchronous task-backed execution library infers data dependencies, manages memory movement, exposes branch and stage-level concurrency. Evaluated on four representative scientific datasets.
nv: First heterogeneous compression framework enabling rapid assembly of custom error-bounded pipelines with high performance and quality trade-off control.
th: Flexible heterogeneous compression pipeline framework

t: Integrating Distributed SQL Query Engines with Object-Based Computational Storage
pb: Object storage systems (S3, MinIO) support only basic in-storage filtering, forcing complex operators (aggregation, top-N) to execute at compute layer, causing excessive data movement and query latency.
me: Presto-OCS connector analyzes distributed SQL execution plans to identify operator pushdown eligibility. Offloads complex operators (aggregation, top-N, joins) to OCS for in-storage execution. Evaluated on real-world HPC analytics queries and TPC-H benchmark.
nv: First integration of advanced in-storage query operators with distributed SQL engine (Presto), achieving substantial data movement reduction and speedup.
th: In-storage query processing for distributed analytics

t: PerfAnalyzer: Revealing Performance Trends using Version Oriented Visual Analysis of Scientific Software
pb: Understanding performance behavior of scientific software across versions and configurations is difficult. Tracking computational parameters, hardware settings, and outcomes across Git commits and multiple runs is complex, hindering root cause analysis of performance regressions.
me: PerfAnalyzer: interactive dashboard for collecting, managing, and visualizing computational parameters across Git commits. Automatically tracks input/output parameters, hardware/software configurations, and performance metrics. Demonstrated on CloverLeaf mini-application across multiple versions.
nv: First interactive dashboard for version-oriented visual analysis of HPC software performance evolution, enabling correlation between code changes and performance outcomes.
th: Version-oriented performance analysis for scientific software

t: Overcoming Dynamic I/O Boundaries: a Double-Sided Streaming Methodology with dispel4py and CAPIO
pb: Workflow orchestration systems struggle with strict I/O boundaries that enforce file synchronization barriers between workflow phases, limiting the ability to implement end-to-end streaming across multi-stage applications.
me: Introduce a double-sided streaming methodology combining control-plane streaming (dispel4py) with data-plane streaming (CAPIO). Extend CAPIO with a new commit rule for streaming over dynamically generated file sets, enabling hybrid in-memory and file-based dataflows.
nv: Novel commit rule enabling streaming across dynamic file sets without modifying existing workflow logic; seamless integration of control and data-plane streaming without artificial boundaries.
th: I/O Optimization & Workflow Orchestration

t: The (R)evolution of Scientific Workflows in the Agentic AI Era: Towards Autonomous Science
pb: Modern scientific discovery requires coordinating distributed facilities and heterogeneous resources. Researchers act as manual workflow coordinators rather than scientists, limiting discovery velocity and scalability.
me: Propose a conceptual framework charting workflow evolution along two dimensions: intelligence (static to intelligent) and composition (single to swarm). Present architectural blueprint for autonomous, distributed scientific laboratories.
nv: Conceptual framework for agentic AI integration into scientific workflows; evolutionary trajectory from current systems to fully autonomous science platforms.
th: Agentic AI & Autonomous Science

me: Artifact evaluation of ThirstyFLOPS paper examining water usage modeling for HPC systems. Assessment conducted by SC25 Reproducibility Committee.

t: Usability Evaluation of Cloud for HPC Applications
pb: Unclear whether cloud environments (Azure, AWS, GCP) provide equivalent performance and usability for HPC workloads compared to on-premises HPC clusters.
me: Cross-platform usability study: 11 HPC proxy apps/benchmarks across 3 clouds, 6 environments, CPU/GPU configs, scaling to 28,672 CPUs and 256 GPUs, benchmarked against LLNL on-premises clusters.
nv: Comprehensive comparative study of cloud-HPC convergence across multiple platforms, scaling factors, and workload types.
th: Cloud suitability for HPC: cross-platform empirical study

t: State Machine Orchestration of an HPC Workflow in Cloud
pb: Porting HPC workflows between cloud and on-premises environments is non-trivial; existing designs may not efficiently leverage cloud-native orchestration frameworks.
me: Redesign MuMMI ensemble workflow for Kubernetes: progression from traditional HPC to fully portable cloud variant; compare service/filesystem-based vs event-driven orchestration.
nv: Systematic redesign of HPC workflow using event-driven cloud-native patterns; quantified performance and cost improvements from orchestration approach.
th: Cloud-native HPC workflow orchestration via event-driven design

t: GPU Programming for AI Workflow Development on AWS SageMaker: An Instructional Approach
pb: GPU programming education and practical experience with cloud platforms is limited; students need hands-on exposure to GPU architecture and AI agent development on realistic infrastructure.
me: Specialized course (Fall 2024-Spring 2025): GPU architecture fundamentals → GPU programming → RAG and AI agent development on AWS SageMaker. Evaluated via assessments, course surveys, TensorBoard/HPC profilers.
nv: Comprehensive GPU+cloud pedagogical model integrating hardware concepts, parallel programming, and practical AI agent deployment.
th: GPU+cloud computing curriculum for STEM education

t: Performance portable batched linear algebra kernels for transport sweeps using Kokkos
pb: Batched linear algebra kernels for neutron transport sweeps on GPUs require high performance across NVIDIA and AMD architectures; existing libraries may not be optimized for transport kernel patterns.
me: Custom batched GESV solver using Kokkos for performance portability. Optimizations: minimize global memory traffic, maximize compile-time computation. Evaluated on H100 (NVIDIA) and MI300A (AMD).
nv: Custom batched GESV outperforming state-of-the-art libraries; performance portability across NVIDIA/AMD via Kokkos.
th: Performance-portable batched linear algebra for neutron transport using Kokkos

t: ModuLair: Streamlining Python Virtual Environment Management for HPC
pb: Managing Python environments on HPC systems is complex due to toolchains, file system constraints, and diverse user needs; existing solutions lack integrated CLI/GUI support.
me: ModuLair: a modular, metadata-driven Python virtual environment framework supporting both EasyBuild and non-EasyBuild module systems with CLI/GUI integration including Jupyter, Drona Composer, and HPRC Dashboard.
nv: First metadata-driven virtual environment framework seamlessly integrating CLI and GUI interfaces for HPC Python management with automatic module system detection.
th: HPC Software Infrastructure

t: Modular Architecture for High-Performance and Low Overhead Data Transfers
pb: Traditional file transfer tools suffer from resource underutilization and instability due to fixed configurations or monolithic optimization methods; adapting to changing network/system conditions is difficult.
me: AutoMDT: modular data transfer architecture using deep reinforcement learning (PPO agent) to optimize concurrency levels for read, network, and write operations. Lightweight simulator enables offline training (~45 min) without impacting production networks.
nv: First modular data transfer framework using RL for adaptive concurrency optimization with offline training capability via lightweight network-system simulator.
th: Adaptive Data Transfer Optimization

pb: Reproducibility of GPU-accelerated data refactoring requires independent artifact evaluation.
me: Artifact evaluation of SC25 paper 'HP-MDR' by Podhorszki et al., assessing experimental setup and result reproducibility.
nv: Reproducibility report documenting artifact evaluation of high-performance data refactoring study.
th: GPU-Accelerated Data Processing

t: InferA: A Smart Assistant for Cosmological Ensemble Data
pb: Analyzing large-scale scientific datasets (terabyte-scale) is hindered by volume, structural complexity, and need for domain expertise; existing automation tools (PandasAI) require full ingestion and lack structural awareness.
me: InferA: multi-agent system using LLMs to orchestrate analysis. Supervisor agent coordinates specialized agents for data retrieval and analysis phases; engages users interactively to clarify intent.
nv: First multi-agent LLM system for scalable scientific data analysis; supervisor orchestration enables structured querying without full data ingestion.
th: LLM-Based Scientific Data Analysis

t: A Modular, Responsive, and Accessible HPC Dashboard Built upon Open OnDemand
pb: HPC systems have high barriers to entry for non-expert users due to reliance on command-line tools; growing user community requires more accessible interfaces.
me: Modern web-based dashboard built on Open OnDemand framework with redesigned functional pages: announcements, system status, job information, resource usage.
nv: Modular, responsive redesign of HPC dashboard interfaces integrated with Open OnDemand; emphasis on modern design and accessibility.
th: HPC User Interface Design

t: Bridging Performance Portability and Scalability for Plasma Simulations on Heterogeneous Systems
pb: Achieving both portability (run on CPUs and GPUs) and scalability (high performance on each) is challenging due to abstraction overhead; performance portability abstractions like Kokkos can hide hardware capabilities.
me: VPIC 2.0 adopts Kokkos for portability, then mitigates overhead via: (1) enhanced vectorization, (2) platform-targeted particle sorting, (3) optimized memory access patterns.
nv: First demonstration that Kokkos-based particle-in-cell code can match hand-tuned performance on CPUs while achieving superlinear scaling on GPUs.
th: Performance Portability for Scientific Simulations

t: EQSIM Agent: A Conversational AI for Interactive Exploration of Large-scale Earthquake Simulation Data
pb: Large-scale earthquake simulations produce massive datasets that are difficult to explore; researchers lack specialized knowledge or programming skills to extract insights.
me: LLM-based conversational agent (EQSIM Agent) for interactive data exploration. Features natural language querying, vision-based waveform similarity search, and RAG system for literature integration.
nv: First conversational AI specifically designed for earthquake simulation data; combines querying, visualization, and literature-informed retrieval.
th: LLM-Based Scientific Data Exploration

t: Quantifying AWS S3 I/O Performance Boundaries Using the Roofline Model
pb: Understanding performance characteristics of AWS S3 integration with HPC systems using different access methods and patterns
me: Roofline-based analysis of three S3 integration approaches: NFS-mounted Storage Gateway, data migration through Storage Gateway, and direct S3 API transfers
nv: Extension of I/O roofline modeling to characterize operational intensity and bandwidth ceilings for cloud storage access patterns
th: Cloud-HPC Integration & I/O Optimization

t: Fantastic Hardware Counters and How to Find Them: Automating the Detection of Noise-Resilient Performance Counters in HPC
pb: Hardware performance counters are noisy and unreliable for performance modeling on HPC systems
me: Automated tool that: builds experimental setup, runs repeated experiments, analyzes counter noise patterns, ranks counters by resilience
nv: Automated detection and ranking of noise-resilient hardware counters with systematic noise analysis methodology
th: Performance Measurement & Profiling

me: SimAI-Bench: benchmarking tool for one-to-one (colocated) and many-to-one (ensemble) coupled workflows on Aurora

me: SimGrid-based simulation framework with plugin mechanisms

pb: Error-bounded lossy compression degrades compression quality and speed when supporting both progressive and random-access decompression.
me: STZ streaming compression framework with hierarchical partitioning strategy and hierarchical prediction mechanism; enables both progressive and random-access decompression.
nv: First compression framework simultaneously supporting both progressive and random-access decompression; hierarchical strategy mitigates partitioning impact.

t: Rethinking Back Transformation in 2-stage Eigenvalue Decomposition on Heterogeneous Architectures
pb: 2-stage EVD method loses performance advantage over 1-stage when computing eigenvectors via back transformation on GPUs.
me: Replace BLAS3 with BLAS2 operations during bulge-chasing; reorder workflow from backward to parallelism-driven pattern hiding divide-and-conquer latency.
nv: BLAS operation level optimization; parallelism-driven workflow pattern for back transformation.

pb: Memory bandwidth-bound linear solvers with variable matrix row lengths and indirect access patterns; inefficient 512-bit vector register utilization on Intel GPUs.
me: ESIMD-based optimization using efficient vectorization for block-sparse vector computations; optimized for variable block sizes; performance within 10% of bandwidth benchmark peak.

t: HPC-R1: Characterizing R1-like Large Reasoning Models on HPC
pb: Limited understanding of Large Reasoning Model (LRM) training performance and system inefficiencies on HPC systems; complex multi-stage workflows challenging to optimize.
me: HPC-R1: characterization of LRM training stages (SFT, GRPO-based RL, generation, distillation) on NERSC Perlmutter; detailed performance analysis.
nv: First comprehensive LRM training characterization on Top500 HPC system; 19 key observations across all training stages.
th: LLM Training Characterization

t: Network Replay and Consistency Across Testbeds
pb: Shared network testbeds introduce variability (jitter, loss) that degrades experiment fidelity and reproducibility; difficult to quantify testbed quality.
me: Choir: 100 Gbps network replay tool running on commodity hardware with novel consistency metric for cross-testbed comparison.
nv: First 100 Gbps replay tool for shared infrastructures; quantitative consistency metric enables testbed quality assessment.

mx.latency_variability: Order of magnitude increase under high utilization

th: Networking Infrastructure

t: ACTINA: Adapting Circuit-Switching Techniques for AI Networking Architectures
pb: Static electrical switch networks limit bandwidth allocation flexibility and increase power consumption in large-scale AI systems; dynamic allocation is needed.
me: Framework for evaluating OCS in AI systems; two in-workload reconfiguration strategies; multi-dimensional all-to-all topology supporting hybrid parallelism.
nv: First quantitative framework for OCS in AI networks; demonstrates OCS-enabled multi-dimensional topology achieves 1.75x better perf-power than Fat-Tree/3D-Torus.
th: Networking for AI Systems

t: Boosting Scientific Error-Bounded Lossy Compression through Optimized Synergistic Lossy-Lossless Orchestration
pb: Scientific workflows on GPUs produce high-throughput data requiring fast error-bounded compression; existing solutions sacrifice ratio or throughput.
me: cuSZ-Hi: GPU-optimized error-bounded lossy compressor combining optimized interpolation-based prediction and lossless encoding pipelines.
nv: 249% compression ratio improvement over SOTA under same error bound; fully GPU-optimized framework with adaptive prediction.
th: Data Management & Compression

t: TurboFNO: High-Performance Fourier Neural Operator with Fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT on GPU
pb: Fourier Neural Operators execute FFT, filtering, GEMM, and iFFT as separate stages, incurring multiple kernel launches and high memory traffic; lacks architecture-aware optimization.
me: Custom FFT and GEMM kernels from scratch; fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT with shared memory swizzling and zero-padding/pruning built-in.
nv: First fully fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT kernel; matches/exceeds closed-source cuBLAS and cuFFT; 100% shared memory bank utilization.
wl: Fourier Neural Operators for PDE solving
th: GPU Kernel Optimization

t: Applying Surrogate Modeling to Decouple Data Collection and Analysis from Simulation for Accelerated In-Situ Analysis
pb: Traditional in-situ analysis is tightly coupled to simulation timesteps, degrading performance and limiting adaptive control of analysis quality.
me: Online surrogate modeling trained on early-stage simulation data; trained models replace simulation for targeted in-situ analysis enabling asynchronous operation.
nv: First decoupled in-situ analysis via online surrogate modeling; 1.20-3.51x speedup with 83.33-99.60% accuracy retention.
th: In-Situ Analysis & Monitoring

t: Classification of Three-dimensional Electron Diffraction Data with a Large Language Model
pb: Three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) generates hundreds to thousands of molecular structures per sample, but many are inaccurate due to noise and measurement limitations. Manual inspection is time-consuming and labor-intensive.
me: LLM-centric automatic screening method: (1) converts atomic coordinates to topology-only language representation, (2) applies rule-based filtering, (3) fine-tunes LLM on correct vs. artificially-corrupted molecules, (4) groups identical topologies.
nv: Novel application of fine-tuned LLMs to scientific structure classification, using topology-only language representation tailored to 3D ED data.
th: LLM-based automated screening for scientific data analysis

t: Do Large Language Models Speak Scientific Workflows?
pb: Limited understanding of LLM capabilities for configuring, annotating, and translating scientific workflows. LLMs may lack sufficient training data on workflow-specific tasks.
me: Experimental study evaluating open- and closed-source LLMs on three workflow-specific experiments using state-of-the-art workflow systems.
nv: First systematic study of LLM applicability to scientific workflow tasks, identifying capability gaps and performance variations across systems.
th: LLM capabilities and limitations for scientific workflow management

t: InferCT: An Efficient and Generalizable Framework to Enable 3D Machine Learning for Computed Tomography
pb: 3D deep learning models for CT inference require large GPU memory, limiting practical deployment. Existing approaches struggle with dataset size variability and imaging task diversity.
me: InferCT partitions CT volumes into cubic sub-volumes fitting GPU memory, distributing across multiple GPUs. Adds vendor-agnostic optimizations: lock-free shared memory data structure, pipeline execution to hide prefetching/post-processing latency, and parallel data loader.
nv: Vendor-agnostic framework combining volume partitioning with lock-free synchronization and pipelined execution for efficient 3D CT inference.
th: Efficient 3D medical imaging inference on GPUs

t: RedSan: A Redundant Memory Instruction Sanitizer for GPU Programs
pb: Existing GPU profiling tools focus on hotspot identification but miss opportunities for removing redundant instructions in already-optimized CUDA programs.
me: Binary instrumentation-based profiler to identify redundant memory instructions. Instruments optimized CUDA programs to detect unnecessary loads/stores without source-code access. Applied to standard benchmarks (PolybenchGPU, Rodinia, PASTA, DARKNET, LULESH).
nv: First binary instrumentation tool specifically targeting redundant memory instructions in CUDA; achieves >6× speedup by identifying opportunities missed by existing profilers.
th: Identifying redundant memory operations in optimized GPU code

t: Minimizing Power Waste in Heterogenous Computing via Adaptive Uncore Scaling
pb: In GPU-dominant heterogeneous systems, uncore (memory, cache, interconnect) frequencies remain at maximum because scaling only occurs when CPU power nears TDP—a rare event in GPU workloads, wasting power.
me: MAGUS runtime monitors memory access patterns and predicts memory intensity. Detects execution phases and scales uncore frequency accordingly. Handles phase transitions smoothly. Integrates vendor power management features (e.g., NVIDIA DCGM, Intel RAS). User-transparent deployment.
nv: First uncore scaling system aware of GPU-dominant workload phases; 27% energy savings while maintaining <5% performance loss.
th: Adaptive power management for GPU-dominant HPC systems

t: A Fully Autonomous 1.2A Auxiliary Buck DC-DC Converter for Fast Transient Load-on-Demand
pb: A fully autonomous auxiliary buck converter for supplying transient load current is proposed in this paper
me: proposed in this paper
nv: Novel propose approach
th: general-vlsi-design

t: LAMA: A Latency Minimum Resource Constraint Accelerator for CNN Models
pb: Deep learning models, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have become crucial in various domains due to their wide applications and exceptional performance
me: designers to fine-tune area and latency trade-offs based on application-specific requirements
nv: Novel novel approach
th: ai-accelerators

t: Low-Power and Superior Performance Design of Ternary Logic Cells Using CNFET and MOSFET Devices for VLSI Applications
pb: Ternary logic implementation faces challenges in power efficiency and performance
me: Compare CNFET and MOSFET ternary logic cells (NTI, PTI, STI) at 45nm; leverage tunable threshold voltage of CNFETs
nv: CNFET-based ternary logic cells with controllable threshold voltage for improved power efficiency
th: Emerging device technologies

t: Symmetry-Based Synthesis for Interpretable Boolean Evaluation
pb: Boolean function synthesis for >6 inputs intractable; state-of-the-art requires hyper-parameter tuning; poor interpretability
me: Symmetry-based remapping engine inspired by Edward's theory; synthesize functions up to 20 inputs via recursive substructure discovery
nv: Scalable symmetry-based Boolean synthesis reaching 20 inputs with interpretable recursive structures
th: Design automation and logic synthesis

t: K Band High Power Broadband AlGaN/GaN HEMT Balanced Power Amplifier for Satellite Transponder
pb: K-band satellite transponders require high-power, high-efficiency broadband power amplifiers
me: Two-stage AlGaN/GaN HEMT MMIC balanced power amplifier on SiC substrate; 0.15um UMS process
nv: Broadband K-band balanced power amplifier achieving 38dBm output, 32% PAE, 23.6dB gain across 18-22GHz
th: RF/mmW circuits and systems

t: A Low-Power, Low-Noise, High-Performance Re-Convergent Clock Mesh Design for Large AI Compute Clusters
pb: Large AI compute clusters require globally synchronous single-clock-domain design for high performance, but traditional clock networks (flex-H tree, forwarded spine) cannot meet the low-power, low-noise requirements for complex AI processors.
me: Novel re-convergent clock mesh architecture specifically designed for large AI compute clusters. Compared against flex-H tree and forwarded spine topologies via HSPICE simulation and PrimeTime timing analysis.
nv: Re-convergent clock mesh achieving significantly improved quality-of-result (QoR) with 20% better power at target frequency OR 20% higher performance at target voltage.
th: Clock network design for AI accelerators

t: Optimizing Multipliers: An Energy-Efficient Design Using a Novel 3:2 Compressor
pb: Power consumption and speed in multipliers depend critically on partial product addition efficiency. Existing 3:2 compressor designs derived from 4:2 compressors are suboptimal for multiplier applications.
me: Novel 3:2 compressor based on two-stage stacking concept to minimize circuit size while maintaining functionality. Applied to design 4-bit, 8-bit, and 16-bit multipliers.
nv: Two-stage stacking compressor achieving 47.30% average power-delay product improvement over existing 3:2 compressor designs.
th: Efficient arithmetic components for processors

t: A First-Principles-Based Comparative Study Between Pristine and Au-Modified Graphene Nanosheet Towards Acetaldehyde Sensing Performance
pb: Acetaldehyde detection requires highly sensitive gas sensing materials. Pristine graphene has limited sensing capability for volatile organic compounds.
me: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations using Gaussian 09W and GaussView 6.0 to model acetaldehyde adsorption on pristine and Au-doped graphene. Analysis of frontier molecular orbitals, electrostatic potential, electron localization function, density of states, band structure, and Mulliken charges.
nv: Comparative DFT study demonstrating superior acetaldehyde sensing with Au-modified graphene via enhanced electronic properties and stronger adsorption.

mx.adsorption_energy: higher for Au-doped vs. pristine graphene (quantitative values not provided)

th: Nanodevice_Sensing

t: 2D Thermal Contour Modeling of 14 nm SOI FinFET Using Machine Learning for Efficient Thermal Profile Prediction
pb: SOI FinFETs suffer from severe self-heating due to reduced thermal conductivity of silicon-on-insulator substrate. Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations for thermal analysis are time-intensive, limiting rapid device design iteration.
me: ML-based approach combining FEM simulation and machine learning (FSML: FEM-supplemented ML). CNN and VAE models trained on thermal FEM datasets. Datasets generated from Synopsys TCAD FEM simulator for 14 nm SOI FinFET. Evaluation metrics: MSE, accuracy, loss, IoU (Intersection Over Union), SSIM (Structural Similarity).
nv: First CNN/VAE model applied to SOI FinFET thermal profile prediction, combining FEM accuracy with ML computational efficiency.
th: ML_for_Device_Thermal_Design

t: A Study on the Impact of Temperature-Dependent Ferroelectric Switching Behavior in 3D Memory Architecture
pb: Hafnium Zirconium Oxide (HZO) FeRAM in 3D neural network accelerators suffers from thermal stress as on-chip temperatures rise during operation. Temperature-dependent ferroelectric switching behavior has not been well characterized in 3D memory architectures.
me: Experimental device characterization and circuit/architecture-level simulation of HZO-based FeRAM in 3D memory architectures. Study of temperature-dependent polarization switching behavior through thermal impact analysis. Dynamic write voltage optimization exploiting temperature-activated switching mechanisms.
nv: First study exploiting temperature-dependent ferroelectric switching to reduce FeRAM write energy in 3D memory architectures for neural network accelerators.
th: Memory_Architecture_and_Thermal_Design

t: HyCMAx: Power-Efficient Hybrid CMOS-Memristor Based Approximate Dividers for Error-Resilient Applications
pb: Approximate computing traditionally uses CMOS technology; exploring hybrid CMOS-memristor approaches can yield further performance and power gains.
me: Hybrid CMOS-memristor approach for approximate circuit design. Proposes approximate subtractor then uses it to implement restoring divider in hybrid CMOS-memristor topology at 28nm CMOS node.
nv: First exploration of hybrid CMOS-memristor approximate computing for divider circuits; demonstrates feasibility and benefits of memristor integration.
th: Hybrid CMOS-memristor approximate computing for power efficiency

t: Boosting System-on-Chip Performance Through AI-Assisted Optimization Using Compositional Neural Networks
pb: SOC performance verification and pre-silicon optimization involves tuning many parameters (frequency, voltage, routing) to meet targets; manual optimization is time-consuming and error-prone.
me: Three-stage framework: (1) Train neural models at component/cluster interfaces on SOC dataset to predict performance from design parameters, (2) Neural networks guide search algorithm to find optimal configurations, (3) Compositional neural network at SOC level using interface-level parameters.
nv: Application of compositional neural networks to SOC optimization; leverages interface-level models to build system-level predictor without expensive full SOC modeling.
th: AI-assisted design automation for SOC optimization

t: Constructing Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree with Conditional Generative Adversarial Network
pb: RSMT (Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree) construction for nets is NP-complete and computationally expensive; efficient algorithms are critical for physical design.
me: Novel image-to-image translation approach using conditional GAN (cGAN) to generate RSMT. Training dataset: RSMT images with optimal wirelength for randomly generated nets.
nv: First application of cGAN for RSMT construction; formulates tree construction as image-to-image translation problem rather than traditional algorithmic approach.
th: ML-based optimization for physical design

t: Physical Synthesis Optimization Prediction Using Machine Learning
pb: Long EDA tool runtimes act as bottlenecks for design turn-around-time in complex SOC design implementation, requiring designers to wait for complete tool runs to obtain critical Power-Performance-Area (PPA) parameters such as timing slack, critical path depth, leakage power, and area.
me: Supervised machine learning model trained on rich sub-10nm SOC design implementation datasets to predict PPA component data early in the physical synthesis flow. Training leverages actual tool run outcomes from a variety of design scenarios at typical 1 GHz clock speeds.
nv: Application of supervised ML to physical synthesis domain for direct prediction of post-implementation PPA metrics, enabling parallel or pre-tool prediction with 6-10% typical accuracy.
th: AI/ML-accelerated design automation

t: Tunnel Magnetoresistance in Strained L10-FeAu Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junction
pb: Magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) are candidates for spintronic memory and computing. Optimizing TMR (tunnel magnetoresistance) performance requires understanding how strain affects intermetallic ferromagnets. L10-FeAu material properties under strain not well understood.
me: Computational analysis combining Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) technique to model L10-FeAu MTJ. Strain analysis (tensile and compressive) evaluates impact on TMR by examining spin-polarized bands at Fermi surface.
nv: First comprehensive DFT-NEGF analysis of strain effects on TMR in L10-FeAu MTJ, revealing band structure mechanisms governing TMR reduction under strain.
th: Computational materials science for spintronic devices

t: Optimal Respiratory Rate Estimation with mmWave Sensing Using PYNQ System-on-Chip Platform
pb: Non-invasive respiratory rate (RR) monitoring using mmWave requires embedded real-time signal processing. Existing approaches may not achieve high accuracy or require complex signal processing.
me: PYNQ platform-based implementation of range and respiration estimation. Signal processing pipeline: (1) Range FFT (RFFT), (2) Phase extraction and unwrapping, (3) FIR filtering, (4) Multiple RR estimation techniques with optimal weighted combination via quadratic cost function.
nv: Optimized multi-technique RR estimation with weighted ensemble on PYNQ embedded platform achieving high accuracy through algorithmic optimization.
th: Embedded mmWave signal processing for health monitoring

t: Physical Insights into the Leakage Mechanisms Governing the Scaling Trends in 4H-SiC Based Junctionless FETs
pb: Wide bandgap semiconductors like 4H-SiC enable advanced devices for high-voltage and high-temperature applications, but leakage mechanisms differ from silicon. Understanding sub-10nm 4H-SiC junctionless FET leakage is critical for design optimization.
me: 2D device simulation (calibrated) analyzing three main leakage components: (1) GIDL via gate-induced drain leakage (band-to-band tunneling), (2) direct gate tunneling, (3) inefficient volume depletion. Comparison of silicon vs. 4H-SiC physics.
nv: First comprehensive analysis of leakage mechanisms in 4H-SiC ultra-short channel JLFETs revealing dominant mechanisms differ from silicon; direct gate tunneling and volume depletion control leakage in sub-10nm regime.
th: Device physics for wide bandgap scaling

t: Advancing Neural Network Performance with Probabilistic Computing for ReLU Function
pb: Neural networks require efficient ReLU activation functions on hardware. Probabilistic computing (p-bits) offers invertible bidirectional operations but ReLU implementation details for p-circuits are underexplored.
me: Framework for designing p-circuits using p-bits (stochastic bit representations). ReLU design using Hamiltonian method with two variants: (1) AND gate-based, (2) non-imply logic gate-based. Also designs 2x1 multiplexer and AB non-imply logic gate.
nv: P-bit ReLU designs using Hamiltonian method with trade-offs between AND-based and non-imply variants; demonstrates invertible ReLU implementation and graph density optimization.
th: Probabilistic computing for neural network efficiency

t: HapticGuide: Interactive Wearable Braille Guide for Enhancing Visual Education
pb: Visually impaired students struggle to understand complex spatial and geometric concepts due to limitations of traditional tactile graphics and physical models, which lack dynamic, real-time feedback mechanisms.
me: A wearable haptic system comprising: (1) a 15×15 grid touch screen made from Velostat pressure sensors and copper strips; (2) a wearable glove with five coin vibration motors; (3) a cloud-based synchronization system that maps touch inputs to haptic feedback patterns.
nv: Integration of pressure-sensing wearable interface with coordinated haptic feedback for interactive geometric education; cloud-synchronized real-time feedback system for assistive learning.
th: Assistive & Accessible Computing
